state_of_the_art:
As of 2026, the credible pipeline for discovering or identifying kinetics from transport data has four layers, and this project currently sits below the modern bar on three of them.

(1) FORM. Strong-form sparse regression — PDE-FIND (Rudy et al. 2017) and vanilla SINDy, i.e. estimate derivatives pointwise then regress — is no longer state of the art and is treated as a baseline. The weak/integral form is the default: WSINDy for PDEs (Messenger & Bortz, JCP 2021) recovers coefficients to machine precision on clean data and stays robust at SNR approaching 1, by integrating against compactly supported test functions instead of differentiating. Fourier Weak SINDy (L4DC 2026) closes the last hand-tuned knob by picking test-function frequencies from a multitaper spectral estimate. For the narrower problem of estimating parameters of a KNOWN structure, WENDy (Bortz, Messenger & Dukic 2023) does weak-form errors-in-variables estimation with no forward solves, often orders of magnitude faster and more accurate than solver-in-the-loop least squares for stiff systems.

(2) MODEL CLASS. Implicit and rational dynamics require SINDy-PI (Kaheman et al. 2020); polynomial libraries cannot represent a rational isotherm. Sparse regression with control (SINDy-c) covers driven systems.

(3) UNCERTAINTY. A single thresholded coefficient vector is no longer a publishable output. Ensemble-SINDy (Fasel et al. 2022) gives per-term inclusion probabilities via bagging at ~the cost of plain SINDy; UQ-SINDy (Hirsh et al. 2022) gives full posteriors with spike-and-slab or horseshoe priors. In the chemical-engineering line, ADoK-S/W (Digital Discovery 2024) select among candidate rate laws by an information criterion over a Pareto front, PI-ADoK (2025) adds hard physical constraints plus Metropolis-Hastings UQ, and DASyR-LLM (2026) uses an LLM in the SR loop to cut iterations-to-ground-truth by 42-79%. Derivative-free domain-informed sparse kinetics (Prabhu et al., IECR 2025) is the reactor-exit-data analogue of the weak-form argument.

(4) IDENTIFIABILITY FIRST. The mature practice is to establish identifiability BEFORE attempting discovery. Structural identifiability by differential algebra is routine for ODEs (StructuralIdentifiability.jl, DAISY) and has now reached PDEs (Byrne et al. 2024; Browning et al. 2024 for reaction-advection-diffusion). Practical identifiability is done by profile likelihood (Raue et al. 2009), whose flat / one-sided-plateau / two-sided-decay trichotomy is the standard reporting format, and by Fisher-information geometry, where the sloppy-model literature (Transtrum et al. 2015) supplies the vocabulary (stiff vs sloppy directions, hyper-ribbon eigenvalue spectra, manifold-boundary model reduction).

Domain-specifically, the adsorption literature settled this question before the ML literature arrived. Knox et al. (IECR 2016) show experimentally that D_L and the LDF coefficient cannot be reliably extracted from an exit breakthrough curve — non-plug flow and channelling dominate the exit signal, D_L correlations disagree by 2-3x, and for steep isotherms the fitted k came out ~50x off correlation values — and they recommend interior axial concentration and temperature profiles instead. Sircar & Hufton (2000) show the LDF coefficient is a lumped, process-dependent quantity rather than an intrinsic material property. The accepted way to obtain a kinetic parameter is therefore an independent small-sample experiment: ZLC (Brandani, Adsorption 2021), frequency response, or gravimetric uptake. FIM/D-optimal design of adsorption experiments is established for equilibrium parameters (Kober et al. 2019, 2021) but is notably under-developed for the kinetic parameter in a column — a real gap.

On KANs: the one task where KANs are documented to beat MLPs at matched budget is symbolic regression (Hou et al. 2407.11075); everywhere else they underperform at 1.36-100x the cost, with a literature-wide absence of statistical rigour around B-spline training instability. KAN 2.0 (Liu & Tegmark 2024) is the reference pipeline for symbolic extraction, and SRBench (La Cava et al. 2021) is the benchmark any SR method claim must be scored against.
implications: The L6 result is correct but under-argued, and the literature has already said it. Knox et al. 2016 (adsorption-specific, experimental) and Sircar & Hufton 2000 (theoretical) between them already establish that the LDF coefficient is not reliably extractable from a breakthrough curve and is not an intrinsic material property. As written, our contribution reads as rediscovery. Reframed as a QUANTITATIVE identifiability map over Damkohler number — 'here is exactly where in Da-space the kinetic parameter carries signal, measured on 988 simulations' — it becomes a genuine addition to that literature rather than an echo of it.

The sampled Damkohler regime, not the joint-vs-separate architecture, is what L6 actually measured. Recomputed from results/identifiability.json: Da = k_LDF * t_final has p05 = 121, median = 628, p95 = 3314 across all 988 conditions, and in 44.0% of conditions the PEAK LDF driving force |q*-q| never exceeds 1% of q_max. The system is in the local-equilibrium limit essentially everywhere. The classical kinetic/mass-transfer transition sits at Da of order 0.1-100. At Da ~ 600 there is nothing about k in the data, so 'separate identification does not beat joint identification' is, in this dataset, a statement about the sampling and not about the hypothesis. This is the strongest single criticism available against the project's primary pre-registered result, and it is one we can fix rather than concede.

Our surviving kinetic estimator is strong-form and single-shot, which is the exact method the 2021-2026 literature exists to replace. identify_kinetics.estimate_k_structured differentiates q with np.gradient and regresses; identify_kinetics.stridge reports one thresholded vector per condition. The weak form (WSINDy/WENDy) is standard for the first, and inclusion probabilities (Ensemble-SINDy/UQ-SINDy) are standard for the second. This matters even though we correctly diagnosed the failure as signal-vs-error (B21: exact driving force peaks at 0.061 mol/kg against fingerprint reconstruction error 0.22-0.47 mol/kg, i.e. error is 5-25x the signal) — because that diagnosis currently rests on one estimator, and a weak-form replicate would make it unfalsifiable rather than merely plausible.

The isotherm-fingerprint problem is an errors-in-variables problem and should be named as one. Our regressor for k treats q*_obs as a known regressor when it carries 0.22-0.47 mol/kg of error against a 0.061 mol/kg signal. WENDy's iteratively-reweighted errors-in-variables formulation is the published, citable treatment of exactly this. Naming the structure (EIV) rather than describing the symptom raises the methodological register of the whole section.

There is a derivable analytic result sitting unclaimed. In the Henry (linear-isotherm) limit our column with Danckwerts inlet, axial dispersion and LDF exchange is a linear reaction-advection-diffusion system observed at the boundary. Its outlet response has a closed-form Laplace transform, and the classical moment result is that the second central moment depends on D_L and k only through a single lumped HETP-like group (roughly 2D_L/v plus a mass-transfer term ~ 2v K'/(k(1+K')^2)). That yields a PROVEN structural statement — D_L and k are confounded in the exit curve, only one combination is identifiable — which explains the empirical R^2 = -0.61 from first principles, connects to Browning et al. 2024 and Byrne et al. 2024, and is far more durable than any regression statistic. This is the highest-value single paragraph the paper is currently missing.

The descriptors -> k_LDF R^2 = -0.61 claim has a dangerous hole that must be closed explicitly. In the generator, k_LDF is presumably drawn independently of the isotherm shape parameters. If so, no function of isotherm descriptors can predict it, and R^2 <= 0 is arithmetic rather than physics; the negative value merely records regressor overfitting. In real materials k does correlate with crystal/pellet size and pore structure, so the synthetic finding may not transfer at all. The paper must state the generative independence in plain words and narrow the claim to what survives: 'k is not recoverable from the DYNAMICS we observe, at the Damkohler numbers we sampled' — a claim that is about the physics of the observation, not about the sampler.

The whole ladder has a plausible unifying explanation it has not yet articulated: this is a sloppy model. Retraction A17 records that three independent function classes are flat in rank while the POD floor falls 28.7x, that only mode 1 is well predicted (R^2 = 0.946) with median R^2 = -0.014 beyond mode 24, and that DeepONet at any p performs like a 4-mode oracle. Add k_LDF being unrecoverable and the picture is a Fisher information matrix with one or two stiff directions (front arrival time, equilibrium capacity) and a long sloppy tail. Computing the FIM eigenspectrum over the 11 generative parameters at a few representative conditions would convert seven separate negative results into one positive structural claim, in the established vocabulary of Transtrum/Sethna. That reframing is likely worth more to a top-tier venue than any individual rung.

The SINDy slot vacated by retraction A7 should be refilled with a real unknown, not with a recovery of the planted law. Rediscovering dq/dt = k(q*-q) from data we generated with dq/dt = k(q*-q) is a recovery benchmark, and must be labelled as such if kept. The genuinely unknown function in this project is the two-wave warp: t_lo(z) and t_hi(z) as functions of the observable descriptors. It is low-dimensional (4 modes), it is where the live 2.17x headroom is (predicted-warp 0.0508 vs oracle 0.0233), and it is exactly the regime where symbolic regression is documented to be competitive. A symbolic warp law would be a discovery, would be interpretable, and would plausibly extrapolate to novel materials better than the current HGB.

L3's anti-KAN verdict is well-supported but must be scoped. The one documented KAN advantage over MLPs at matched budget is symbolic regression (Hou et al.), which L3 did not test. Our claim should be stated as an accuracy-at-matched-parameters claim about field regression, not as a general verdict on KANs. Conversely, our own B22 evidence (10/45 DeepOKAN training collapses vs 0/45 DeepONet; gradient norm collapsing to 1.2e-11 by step 150 at the wrong learning rate) is a direct empirical instance of the training-instability-under-reporting that the critical-assessment paper alleges of the KAN literature — that is a contribution worth stating loudly, with a citation.

The paper currently has no answer to 'so how would anyone actually get k_LDF?' The published answer is: not from the column. ZLC, frequency response, or gravimetric uptake on ~10 mg of sample, which suppresses external resistances and decouples kinetics from equilibrium. If a column must be used, Knox et al.'s prescription is interior axial concentration AND temperature probes, plus a separate non-adsorbing tracer run to fix D_L before k is fitted. One paragraph with these three citations turns a bare negative into practical guidance, and pre-empts the referee question.
risks_to_our_claims: FATAL IF UNADDRESSED — 'Your L6 verdict is an artefact of your Damkohler sampling.' With Da spanning 121-3314 (median 628) and peak driving force below 1% of q_max in 44% of conditions, the kinetic parameter leaves no measurable trace. A referee will say the rung tested the local-equilibrium limit and reported the answer as if it were about joint-vs-separate learning. The pre-registered protocol makes this worse, not better: freezing a hypothesis does not immunise it against a design that cannot resolve the effect. This is already listed as the project's own open item 6, which means we know and have not acted.

'You rediscovered Knox et al. 2016.' The non-identifiability of the LDF coefficient from a breakthrough curve is a published, experimentally demonstrated result a decade old, in a mainstream adsorption journal. If we present k_LDF unrecoverability as a finding rather than as a quantitative refinement of a known result, we look unaware of our own field's literature — which is especially damaging given RETRACTIONS.md is explicitly a document about epistemic care.

'The LDF coefficient is not an intrinsic material property, so H1 was ill-posed.' Sircar & Hufton (2000) establish that k lumps process conditions into a single number. If k is not a material property, then 'identify the material's kinetic object separately from its equilibrium object' has no well-defined target, and the negative result is definitional rather than empirical.

'R^2 = -0.61 for descriptors -> k_LDF is trivially true by construction of your generator.' If k_LDF is sampled independently of the isotherm descriptors, no regressor can do better than the mean and a negative R^2 just measures overfitting. This turns a headline result into an arithmetic identity. It must be disclosed and the claim narrowed before a referee finds it.

'You used a 2017 method badly, then replaced it with a 2017 method used correctly.' A7 retracts a PDE-FIND-style pipeline; the replacement is still strong-form np.gradient plus hand-rolled thresholded ridge. Given that weak-form discovery has been the standard since 2021 and weak-form parameter estimation since 2023, the replacement does not reach current practice, and the retraction narrative therefore ends in the wrong place.

'No uncertainty on any identification result.' k_hat is reported with no confidence interval; the sparse selection is reported as a per-condition frequency of a single thresholded draw. Ensemble inclusion probabilities and profile-likelihood intervals are both standard and cheap. This also violates the project's own standing rule 3 in spirit (no single-draw numbers in tables).

'You claim non-identifiability but never did an identifiability analysis.' We report an ML statistic (R^2) and a physical scale argument (driving force vs fingerprint error). Neither is a profile likelihood, a Fisher information rank/eigenvalue analysis, or a structural identifiability test. Reviewers in the identifiability community will not accept an R^2 as evidence of non-identifiability — a poor regressor and a non-identifiable parameter produce the same number.

'L3 says KANs lose, but you tested them only where they were never claimed to win.' The documented KAN advantage is symbolic regression / interpretability, not field regression accuracy. An unscoped anti-KAN claim invites a straightforward rebuttal, and the project has already retracted one over-broad architecture claim (A12).

'Your isotherm fingerprint is not a real measurement.' The fingerprint is computed from the same analytic q* that generated the data, then interpolated. A referee can argue that the entire equilibrium/kinetic asymmetry (equilibrium R^2 = 0.93-0.96, kinetics -0.61) is an artefact of how the fingerprint was synthesised, since real isotherm measurements carry systematic as well as interpolation error.

'The learning-curve result contradicts your own L1 verdict and you buried it.' learning_curve.log shows 1.82x improvement (0.0929 -> 0.0509) from 12 to 48 training materials, not saturated. That cuts directly against L1's 'more data is eliminated' on the material axis, and the scale-up dataset (data/parametric_scale) is incomplete at ~1457 of 4080 files with no manifest. Publishing L1's verdict while sitting on an unfinished experiment that undercuts it is the single most reputationally dangerous thing in the repository, given what RETRACTIONS.md promises about the project's standards.

concrete_actions.action: Re-sample k_LDF so the dataset spans the identifiable kinetic regime, then re-run L6 as a Damkohler-resolved experiment. Draw k log-uniformly so the number of transfer units N = k*L/v spans roughly 1 to 300 (covering Da ~ 1-50 as well as the current near-equilibrium band), and report the separate-minus-joint gap as a FUNCTION of Da rather than as one pooled number. Keep the existing 988-run dataset as the 'local equilibrium' stratum so nothing already reported is invalidated.
concrete_actions.rationale: Measured from results/identifiability.json, current Da_run is p05 = 121, median = 628, p95 = 3314, with 44.0% of conditions never exceeding 1% of q_max in driving force. At those values k is physically absent from the data, so H1 was tested where it cannot be resolved. This converts the project's most attackable result into its most interesting one: instead of 'separate identification does not help', the paper gets 'separate identification helps only for Da below X, and we measured X' — a curve, not a null. It also directly discharges the project's own open item 6.

concrete_actions.action: Derive and report the analytic identifiability statement for the linearized column. In the Henry limit, take the Laplace transform of the Danckwerts + dispersion + LDF system, extract the first and second moments of the outlet response, and show explicitly that D_L and k_LDF enter only through one lumped group. State the resulting structural conclusion — from the exit curve alone, only that combination is identifiable — and cite Browning et al. (2024) and Byrne et al. (2024) for the general PDE machinery, Knox et al. (2016) for the experimental confirmation.
concrete_actions.rationale: This replaces an empirical regression statistic with a theorem. It explains R^2 = -0.61 from first principles, it is immune to the 'your generator made k independent of the descriptors' objection because it is about the observation operator rather than the sampler, and it gives the paper a genuinely analytical result in a lens where it currently has none. It is also cheap: pen-and-paper plus a numerical check against the existing solver.

concrete_actions.action: Disclose the generative independence of k_LDF and narrow the descriptors-based claim. Add explicit text stating that k_LDF is sampled independently of the isotherm parameters in the generator, that R^2 <= 0 for descriptors -> k is therefore expected by construction, and that the claim the paper makes is the narrower and defensible one about recoverability from observed DYNAMICS at the sampled Damkohler numbers. Note that in real adsorbents k does correlate with particle and pore structure, so the synthetic asymmetry may not transfer.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is a one-paragraph fix for what would otherwise be a devastating referee comment, and the project's own retraction culture makes silence on it much worse than disclosure. It costs nothing and removes an entire attack surface.

concrete_actions.action: Run profile-likelihood practical identifiability for k_LDF on ~10 representative conditions spanning the new Da range, and report the profiles with the standard flat / one-sided-plateau / two-sided-decay classification and threshold-based confidence intervals (Raue et al. 2009). Do the same for D_L on the same conditions to demonstrate the confounding.
concrete_actions.rationale: Turns 'a regressor got R^2 = -0.61' into a proper identifiability result with intervals, in the format the identifiability community recognises. At 4.2 s per solver run, a 40-point profile over 10 conditions plus re-optimisation of nuisance parameters is a few CPU-hours. It is the cheapest available upgrade in scientific register per unit effort.

concrete_actions.action: Compute the Fisher information matrix over the 11 generative parameters at several representative conditions and report its eigenvalue spectrum, the eigenvector loadings, and where k_LDF sits. Frame the result in sloppy-model language (Transtrum et al. 2015): stiff directions vs sloppy tail, and connect it explicitly to A17's finding that three independent function classes are flat in rank while the POD floor falls 28.7x.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is the unifying theoretical claim the ladder currently lacks. If k_LDF loads on the smallest eigenvalue and front-arrival/capacity load on the largest, the paper can state one structural fact that explains L1's data plateau, L2's capacity saturation, L5's operator flatness, and L6's null simultaneously. That is the difference between seven negative results and one positive theory of why the problem is hard.

concrete_actions.action: Re-implement the kinetic estimator in weak form. Replace np.gradient(q, t) + ordinary least squares with a WENDy-style estimator: integrate dq/dt = k(q*_obs - q) against compactly supported test functions, integrate by parts to move the derivative onto the test function, and solve the errors-in-variables regression by IRLS. Use PySINDy's weak-form module rather than hand-rolling, and report both estimators side by side.
concrete_actions.rationale: Our conclusion that the failure is signal-vs-error rather than estimator noise (B21) currently rests on a single strong-form estimator, which is exactly the estimator the field replaced. If the weak-form estimator also fails, the conclusion becomes unassailable; if it succeeds, we have found a real result and avoided publishing a false negative. Either outcome is worth having, and it also removes the 'you hand-rolled a library that once had condition number 1.07e44' objection.

concrete_actions.action: Add the experimental-design paragraph: state that the published way to obtain k_LDF is an independent small-sample measurement (ZLC, frequency response, gravimetric uptake) rather than a breakthrough fit, and that if a column must be used the requirements are interior axial concentration and temperature probes plus a separate non-adsorbing tracer run to fix D_L first. Cite Brandani (2021), Knox et al. (2016), Sircar & Hufton (2000), Glueckauf (1955).
concrete_actions.rationale: The paper currently ends its identifiability discussion on a negative with no practical consequence. This converts it into guidance and demonstrates command of the adsorption literature, which is the reader community most likely to referee it. It is also the point at which the interior temperature wave should be flagged as the observable that carries kinetic information the exit concentration curve does not — which is a testable prediction our solver can check immediately.

concrete_actions.action: Refill the vacated A7 slot with symbolic regression of the two-wave warp rather than recovery of the planted kinetic law. Run PySR (dimensionally constrained, with the known limits: Henry behaviour as c -> 0, constant-pattern as N -> infinity) on the start/logspan warp parameterisation to find closed-form t_lo and t_hi as functions of the observable descriptors, and compare against the current HGB warp predictor.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is the one genuinely unknown low-dimensional function in the project and it sits on the live frontier: predicted-warp nRMSE is 0.0508 against an oracle 0.0233, i.e. 2.17x headroom, and the current predictor is an uninterpretable HGB at R^2 = +0.895/+0.919. Symbolic regression is documented to be competitive precisely in this low-dimensional, physically-constrained regime. A symbolic warp law would be a discovery rather than a recovery, would be interpretable, and would plausibly extrapolate to novel materials better than a tree ensemble.

concrete_actions.action: If any sparse-selection result stays in the paper, report it with ensemble inclusion probabilities (Ensemble-SINDy) or posterior inclusion probabilities (UQ-SINDy) instead of the per-condition frequency of a single thresholded draw. Explicitly label the LDF-recovery experiment as a RECOVERY BENCHMARK (can the method recover a law we planted, under our stated noise model?) rather than as discovery.
concrete_actions.rationale: A single thresholded coefficient vector is not a 2026-acceptable discovery output, and it conflicts with the project's own standing rule against single-draw numbers. The relabelling is free and forestalls the obvious objection that discovering a law you generated is circular — an objection the project already leveled at itself in A7 and should not re-earn.

concrete_actions.action: Choose the operating conditions by FIM/D-optimal design for k_LDF rather than by hand. Compute the sensitivity of the observables (exit curve, and separately the interior thermal wave) to k across the operating envelope, and select the per-material condition set to maximise det(FIM) for k. Report the achieved information gain against the current hand-chosen 17 conditions.
concrete_actions.rationale: D-optimal design is established in adsorption for EQUILIBRIUM parameters (Kober et al. 2019, 2021) and is notably absent for the kinetic parameter in a column. Doing it is a self-contained methodological novelty that fits the paper's existing framing, is entirely simulation-based so costs no lab time, and would give the re-run L6 a principled design instead of another hand-picked grid.

concrete_actions.action: Close L3's interpretability gap on its own terms: test KAN symbolic extraction (KAN 2.0 / pykan) on the low-dimensional warp problem, scored against PySR and against the HGB baseline, with multiple seeds and reported variance. Scope L3's existing claim in the text to accuracy-at-matched-parameters on field regression.
concrete_actions.rationale: The documented KAN advantage is symbolic regression, the one axis L3 did not test, so the current claim is broader than the evidence. Running the missing test either strengthens the verdict across the axis that matters most to KAN proponents, or finds the one place KANs earn their cost. Reporting seed variance also lets us state, with our own B22 evidence (10/45 collapses vs 0/45), that KAN training instability is systematically under-reported in the literature — a claim the critical-assessment paper supports and that would be a genuine contribution.

concrete_actions.action: Verify or drop the 2026 catalytic-kinetics review (ScienceDirect PII S2211339826000158) before citing it, and obtain full text for Sircar & Hufton (2000) and Brandani (2021) to confirm the sentence-level claims attributed to them here.
concrete_actions.rationale: I verified those three by bibliographic record and search summary, not by reading the full text. Given this project's retraction discipline, no citation should enter the manuscript on that basis — and one hallucinated or misattributed reference would do more damage to this specific paper's credibility than any technical defect in it.

lens: Machine-learning and neural-operator surrogates for adsorption / chromatography / PSA-TSA breakthrough curves and fixed-bed columns

papers.citation: Beatrice Ceccanti, Mattia Galanti, Ivo Roghair, Martin van Sint Annaland, "Deep Operator Networks for Surrogate Modeling of Cyclic Adsorption Processes with Varying Initial Conditions" (36 pp., 11 figs, cs.LG)
papers.what_it_shows: DeepONet surrogate for Temperature-Vacuum Swing Adsorption (TVSA) cyclic PDE simulation; trains on heterogeneous initial conditions and reports accurate prediction both inside and beyond the training distribution, including unseen functional forms of the initial condition. No quantitative metric in the abstract; no baseline comparison mentioned; generalization axis is initial/operating conditions, NOT held-out materials.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the closest published thing to our L5 rung and it is seven months old. Our claim cannot be 'first DeepONet for adsorption columns'. But it also does NOT do a material-transfer split, reports no floor, no seeds, no CIs, and no negative result — so our contribution (leave-material-out clustered split, POD n-width floor as denominator, basis-vs-coefficient decomposition) survives, provided we cite this and position against it explicitly.

papers.citation: Samuel Lanthaler, Roberto Molinaro, Patrik Hadorn, Siddhartha Mishra, "Nonlinear Reconstruction for Operator Learning of PDEs with Discontinuities" (ICLR 2023)
papers.what_it_shows: Proves rigorous LOWER approximation bounds showing that any method with a LINEAR reconstruction step — DeepONet, PCA-Net, POD-based ROMs — fails to efficiently approximate solution operators of hyperbolic / advection-dominated PDEs with discontinuities. Introduces shift-DeepONet (nonlinear reconstruction). Shows empirically on advection, inviscid Burgers and compressible Euler that FNO and shift-DeepONet circumvent the barrier that binds linear-reconstruction methods.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the theoretical anchor our L5 is missing, and simultaneously our single biggest referee risk. Our measured bottleneck (params->coefficient map dead beyond ~5 modes, DeepONet flat in p) is exactly the regime their theorem describes. A referee will ask why we tested only the two architectures the theorem predicts will fail, and not the two it predicts will succeed (FNO, shift-DeepONet). Citing it turns L5 from an unexplained null into a domain confirmation of a theorem — but only if we also run the escape routes.

papers.citation: Alexander Heinlein, Ben Taraz, "The Error of Deep Operator Networks Is the Sum of Its Parts" (36 pp., 15 figs)
papers.what_it_shows: Decomposes DeepONet error into branch and trunk contributions and into per-mode contributions. Finds the approximation error is DOMINATED BY THE BRANCH NETWORK once the internal (basis) dimension is sufficiently large, and finds spectral bias: coefficients of dominant low-frequency modes are learned well, higher modes poorly. Experiments on KdV and Burgers; compares shared-branch vs stacked architectures.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is our L5 bottleneck result, published independently six months ago, on canonical PDEs. It is the most serious novelty threat to what CONTINUE_HERE.md calls 'the strongest result in the project'. We must cite it and re-scope our claim: our contribution is no longer 'we discovered the coefficient map is the bottleneck' but 'we quantify it against a measured n-width floor on an engineering multiphysics system, under a material-transfer split, with an oracle-rank calibration (128 basis functions buy the accuracy of 4)'. The oracle-equivalent-rank framing appears to be ours; the qualitative finding is not.

papers.citation: Kasturi Nagesh Pai, Vinay Prasad, Arvind Rajendran, "Generalized, Adsorbent-Agnostic, Artificial Neural Network Framework for Rapid Simulation, Optimization, and Adsorbent Screening of Adsorption Processes", Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research
papers.what_it_shows: The reference 'material-transfer' ANN surrogate in the adsorption-process field: isotherm parameters enter as network inputs so one trained network covers many adsorbents, used for PSA/VSA simulation, optimization and adsorbent screening. ~59 citations. NOTE: ACS blocked full-text retrieval (HTTP 403); metadata confirmed independently via Crossref and Semantic Scholar; I could not read how their held-out set is constructed or their reported error.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the domain baseline our paper is actually competing with, and it is currently uncited and un-benchmarked in our manuscript. Any adsorption-community referee will ask 'how does this compare to the adsorbent-agnostic ANN framework?' We must obtain the paper, state precisely whether their split is random-over-isotherm-parameters (interpolation) or clustered-by-material (our transfer setting), and make that distinction one of our stated contributions.

papers.citation: Kasturi Nagesh Pai, et al., "Experimental validation of an adsorbent-agnostic artificial neural network (ANN) framework for the design and optimization of cyclic adsorption processes", Separation and Purification Technology
papers.what_it_shows: Experimental validation of the adsorbent-agnostic ANN framework above (metadata from Crossref only; I did not read the abstract).
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Directly relevant to our open item #2 (no experimental validation). It establishes that the field's expected bar for this class of paper now includes experimental closure. It is also the natural template for the cheapest credible fix: validate the SOLVER against a published breakthrough curve, then keep the surrogate-vs-solver error budget separate.

papers.citation: Sai Gokul Subraveti, Zukui Li, Vinay Prasad, Arvind Rajendran, "Physics-Based Neural Networks for Simulation and Synthesis of Cyclic Adsorption Processes", Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research
papers.what_it_shows: Physics-based / physics-constrained neural networks for cyclic adsorption process simulation and synthesis (metadata verified via Crossref; abstract not retrieved).
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the domain-specific prior for our L4/L4b rung ('physics as a loss', and 'hard bounds beat soft penalties'). Our L4b result — that hard output bounds are the best single intervention and that the PDE residual HURTS once bounds exist — is a direct, quantified refinement of this line of work and should be framed against it rather than against generic PINN papers.

papers.citation: Zicheng Meng, Tingting Liu, Lijing Mu, Cenfan Liu, Xizhong Chen, "Physics-Informed DeepONet for Fixed-Bed Reactor Design and Multiobjective Optimization", Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 65(10), 5349-5363
papers.what_it_shows: Physics-informed DeepONet applied to fixed-bed reactor (packed column) design and multiobjective optimization, published March 2026 (metadata verified via Crossref; abstract not retrievable, ACS blocked).
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Combined with Ceccanti et al., this shows the 'PI-DeepONet for packed columns' niche closed during 2026. Two independent groups got there first. Our differentiator must be the falsification design and the transfer split, not the architecture. Must be cited or a referee will find it.

papers.citation: Julius Reiss, Philipp Schulze, Jörn Sesterhenn, Volker Mehrmann, "The shifted proper orthogonal decomposition: A mode decomposition for multiple transport phenomena" (published SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2018)
papers.what_it_shows: Introduces shifted POD (sPOD): decomposes a field into several co-moving frames, one per transport phenomenon, and determines MULTIPLE transport velocities. Explicitly designed for exactly the situation where a single shift cannot align two waves.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Our 'two-wave warp' is a special case of an idea that has existed since 2015 and is standard in transport-dominated model reduction. This is the largest framing risk on the project's one positive result. Our defensible novelty is narrower and still real: applying a TWO-SHIFT normalising warp (which also removes transition width, not just arrival time) to Type V adsorption, measuring the 31->13 n-width collapse, and — crucially — quantifying how much of the gain survives learned front prediction. But we must stop describing it as new and cite sPOD as the parent method.

papers.citation: Philipp Krah, Arthur Marmin, Beata Zorawski, Julius Reiss, Kai Schneider, "A robust shifted proper orthogonal decomposition: Proximal methods for decomposing flows with multiple transports"
papers.what_it_shows: Modern sPOD with proximal / low-rank optimization for flows with multiple simultaneous transports.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The state of the art in the exact class our two-wave warp belongs to. It is the method our warp should be benchmarked against on our own data: sPOD would decompose the Henry wave and the cooperative shock into two co-moving fields rather than warping to a single normalised sigma coordinate, and it may recover more than 13 modes' worth of structure.

papers.citation: Beata Zorawski, Shubhaditya Burela, Philipp Krah, Arthur Marmin, Kai Schneider, "Automated transport separation using the neural shifted proper orthogonal decomposition" (ECCOMAS 2024)
papers.what_it_shows: Trains two sub-networks jointly — one learning the TRANSPORTS, one learning the co-moving fields — so the shifts do not have to be known a priori. Demonstrated on synthetic data and a wildland-fire model; code on GitHub.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the published remedy for the exact obstruction our project has just relocated to: 'the entire 2.5x is consumed by the error in locating the two fronts'. Our warp_predict.py fits the shifts SEPARATELY (HGB on descriptors, R^2 ~ 0.90) and then reconstructs; neural sPOD trains the shift network and the shape basis end-to-end against reconstruction error, which is exactly the coupling our two-stage pipeline lacks. Strongest single actionable method transfer available to the project right now.

papers.citation: Shubhaditya Burela, Philipp Krah, Julius Reiss, "Parametric model order reduction for a wildland fire model via the shifted POD based deep learning method"
papers.what_it_shows: Parametric sPOD ROM where a neural network predicts both the shift amplitudes and the co-moving mode coefficients as functions of the parameter, for a transport-dominated reactive front problem.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the closest published analogue of our full pipeline (parameters -> front positions -> warped-frame coefficients -> field) in another domain. It is the paper to benchmark our predicted-warp architecture against, and it demonstrates the parametric online phase we have not yet solved.

papers.citation: Tommaso Taddei, "A registration method for model order reduction: data compression and geometry reduction" (SIAM J. Sci. Comput.)
papers.what_it_shows: Canonical registration-based ROM: learn a parameter-dependent mapping that makes the mapped solution manifold amenable to linear compression.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The formal statement of what our warp is. Citing Taddei lets us say precisely what we did (a physically parameterised registration with two landmarks) and lets us report the n-width-before/after as the standard diagnostic of that literature rather than as an ad-hoc measurement.

papers.citation: Nirmal J. Nair, Maciej Balajewicz, "Transported snapshot model order reduction approach for parametric, steady-state fluid flows containing parameter dependent shocks"
papers.what_it_shows: Transports snapshots by a spatially and parametrically dependent transport field before POD, for flows with parameter-dependent shock locations.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Direct precedent for 'the shock moves with the parameter, so remove it before projecting' — the reasoning our co-moving rung used. Also the precedent for our negative result: single-shift transport fails when there are two features moving independently.

papers.citation: Rambod Mojgani, Maciej Balajewicz, "Lagrangian basis method for dimensionality reduction of convection dominated nonlinear flows"
papers.what_it_shows: ROM in a Lagrangian frame where wave-like solutions become low-rank.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Canonical older reference for the co-moving-frame idea; needed so our L5-successor section reads as engaging a literature rather than reinventing it.

papers.citation: Khemraj Shukla, Juan Diego Toscano, Zhicheng Wang, Zongren Zou, George Em Karniadakis, "A comprehensive and FAIR comparison between MLP and KAN representations for differential equations and operator networks" (CMAME 2024)
papers.what_it_shows: Builds PIKANs and DeepOKANs and compares against PINNs and DeepONets under FAIR conditions. B-spline KANs 'lack accuracy and efficiency'; orthogonal-polynomial KANs are comparable but LESS ROBUST, with potential divergence across random seeds.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Already cited in our protocol, and it is the only strong counter-anchor in a KAN literature that is overwhelmingly positive (of ~19 recent arXiv KAN-vs-MLP PDE benchmarks I enumerated, essentially all report KAN winning). Our L3 (MLP beats both KAN families at matched parameters at every budget, 8/9 significant) and our L5 DeepOKAN collapse rate (10/45 vs 0/45) are independent replications of Shukla's robustness finding on a new domain — that is a genuinely publishable, and currently under-represented, contribution. It is also why L3/L5 will attract hostile review: we should pre-empt by reporting the KAN hyperparameter audit prominently.

papers.citation: Lu Lu, Xuhui Meng, Shengze Cai, Zhiping Mao, Somdatta Goswami, Zhongqiang Zhang, George Em Karniadakis, "A comprehensive and fair comparison of two neural operators (with practical extensions) based on FAIR data" (CMAME 393:114778, 2022)
papers.what_it_shows: 16-benchmark head-to-head of DeepONet and FNO with practical extensions (including POD-DeepONet). FNO degrades significantly on complex geometries and with noise (0.1% noise blows up FNO error while DeepONet is largely unaffected); performance otherwise comparable. Provides theoretical error comparison under matched regularity.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the field-standard template for a 'fair comparison' operator paper and defines the baselines reviewers expect: FNO and POD-DeepONet, neither of which we ran. POD-DeepONet is especially pointed for us — it fixes the trunk to the POD basis and trains only the coefficient map, which is precisely the object we measured as the bottleneck. Running it would let us state the bottleneck claim in the field's own currency.

papers.citation: Jacob Seidman, Georgios Kissas, Paris Perdikaris, George J. Pappas, "NOMAD: Nonlinear Manifold Decoders for Operator Learning", NeurIPS 2022
papers.what_it_shows: Replaces DeepONet's linear (branch-dot-trunk) decoder with a nonlinear decoder that learns finite-dimensional nonlinear submanifolds in function space; outperforms larger linear models and matches SOTA operator learning at much smaller model size on a fluid benchmark. Code available.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The cheapest, most direct falsification of our own L5 conclusion, and therefore the most valuable experiment left in the ladder. If NOMAD at ~200k parameters also sits at ~0.028 on our novel-material split, our 'the coefficient map is the binding constraint' claim becomes very strong. If it breaks the flat-in-p behaviour, our headline needs revising before a referee does it for us.

papers.citation: Y. Zhu, J. Chen, W. Deng, "R-adaptive DeepONet: Learning Solution Operators for PDEs with Discontinuous Solutions Using an R-adaptive Strategy"
papers.what_it_shows: Explicitly targets DeepONet's 'linear reconstruction property' limitation with a moving-mesh (r-adaptive) strategy and reports SUPERLINEAR decay of approximation error with trunk basis size, versus the vanilla linear-reconstruction rate.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: A published method whose headline metric is exactly the curve we measured as flat (error vs number of basis functions p). It is a moving-mesh = warp method inside a DeepONet — i.e. it unifies our two-wave warp result with our L5 result. Strong candidate for 'the one architecture we add to L5 to close the ladder honestly'.

papers.what_it_shows: Two-step DeepONet training: optimize the trunk first with Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization, then train the branch, splitting the optimization into lower-complexity subtasks; gives generalization error estimates in terms of data count, width and sensor count; reports improved stability and generalization (examples include heterogeneous porous-media flow).
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: If the coefficient map is the binding constraint, two-step training is the standard way to isolate and improve it — and it is a stronger DeepONet configuration than the joint-trained one we used. Our own trap #3 ('compare against the STRONGEST competitor config') applies: a referee can argue our DeepONet was not at its strongest. Cheap to add.

papers.what_it_shows: Title and DOI confirmed via Crossref only; SSRN blocked full retrieval (HTTP 403). Judging by title alone it decomposes a breakthrough curve into a SHAPE component and a TIMESCALE component inside a hybrid deep-learning framework, for scale-up prediction.

state_of_the_art:
As of mid-2026 the field splits into three layers, and our study sits in a gap between them.

(1) PROCESS-KPI SURROGATES — the mature, dominant layer. Feed-forward ANNs / GPs / trees map design + operating variables (and, in the best work, isotherm parameters) to cycle KPIs: purity, recovery, productivity, energy, cyclic steady state. The strongest and most-cited line is the Rajendran group's "adsorbent-agnostic" ANN framework (Pai, Prasad & Rajendran, IECR 2020; experimentally validated, Sep. Purif. Technol. 2022) and its physics-constrained sibling (Subraveti et al., IECR 2022). Typical reported performance is R^2 > 0.98 or a few percent on scalar KPIs, with wall-clock reductions of 3-4 orders of magnitude (e.g. optimization from ~15.7 h to ~50 s). These almost never predict fields, almost never report seeds or confidence intervals, and never report a lower bound.

(2) FIELD / PROFILE SURROGATES — thin, and only just arrived. PINNs for chromatography (lumped-kinetic and general rate models, incl. gradient elution and MPC of periodic counter-current chromatography) are the established form, but they are per-system solvers, not cross-material surrogates. Operator learning entered this domain in 2026, essentially simultaneously with our project: DeepONet for cyclic TVSA with varying initial conditions (Ceccanti, Galanti, Roghair & van Sint Annaland, arXiv:2601.09491, Jan 2026) and Physics-Informed DeepONet for fixed-bed reactor design (Meng et al., IECR 65(10):5349-5363, Mar 2026). Hybrid neural-ODE + symbolic-regression discovery of sorption kinetics from breakthrough curves exists (arXiv:2303.13555). In the adjacent reactive-porous-media community, breakthrough-curve prediction from (Da, Pe) has an actual benchmark tradition (arXiv:2204.11719, 2301.04998, 2405.19170) using GPs, tensor methods and greedy kernel methods.

(3) THEORY AND FRAMES — the layer our results actually live in, and the one our manuscript currently under-cites. Lanthaler, Molinaro, Hadorn & Mishra (ICLR 2023) PROVE that linear-reconstruction operator learners (DeepONet, PCA-Net, POD+regressor) cannot efficiently approximate advection-dominated/discontinuous solution operators, and that FNO and shift-DeepONet escape the bound. Heinlein & Taraz (arXiv:2602.21910, Feb 2026) show empirically and analytically that DeepONet error becomes BRANCH-dominated once the internal dimension is large, with spectral bias across modes. The remedy family — registration / shifted-POD / Lagrangian ROMs — is 8-10 years old and mature: sPOD explicitly for MULTIPLE transport phenomena (Reiss et al. 2015/2018), Taddei's registration ROM (2019/2020), transported-snapshot MOR (Nair & Balajewicz 2017), Lagrangian basis (Mojgani & Balajewicz 2017), robust multi-transport sPOD (Krah et al. 2024/25), and neural sPOD that LEARNS the transports jointly with the co-moving fields (Zorawski et al., ECCOMAS 2024).

ON SPLITS — the answer to your specific question. I found no published breakthrough-curve or column-field surrogate that uses a clustered leave-materials-out split with cluster-robust inference. "Adsorbent-agnostic" in the process-ML literature means isotherm parameters are network inputs; the evaluation is over randomly sampled isotherm-parameter vectors, i.e. interpolation inside a parameter box, not transfer to held-out materials. The 2026 DeepONet adsorption papers generalize over initial/operating conditions and functional forms of the input, not over materials. That gap is real and it is our strongest structural claim.

ON NEGATIVE RESULTS — nobody has published our specific ladder. But the two components a referee would call "known" are now published: the KAN-underperforms-and-is-seed-fragile result (Shukla et al., CMAME 2024) and the branch/coefficient-map-dominates result (Heinlein & Taraz 2026). The DeepONet-flat-in-p curve itself I did not find published as a measured result; the closest is R-adaptive DeepONet (arXiv:2408.04157), which cites vanilla DeepONet's linear error decay in trunk basis size as the thing it fixes.

STRONGEST PUBLISHED BASELINE WE SHOULD BE BENCHMARKING AGAINST: for the domain, Pai et al.'s adsorbent-agnostic ANN; for the operator rung, FNO and POD-DeepONet from Lu et al. (CMAME 2022) plus shift-DeepONet/NOMAD as the nonlinear-reconstruction escape; for the warped frame, sPOD / neural sPOD.
implications: OUR STUDY IS NOVEL, BUT NOT WHERE THE MANUSCRIPT CURRENTLY THINKS IT IS. The novel core is: (a) the clustered leave-material-out split for column FIELDS, which appears to be unprecedented in this domain; (b) scoring every arm against a measured POD/n-width floor so 'x above the floor' is meaningful; (c) the pre-registered falsification ladder with a calibrated cluster bootstrap and a public retraction ledger; (d) the oracle-equivalent-rank calibration ('128 basis functions buy the accuracy of four'). The parts that are NOT novel any more: DeepONet for adsorption columns (Jan 2026), the branch/coefficient-map bottleneck (Feb 2026), multi-frame warping of transport-dominated fields (2015).

L5 HAS A STRUCTURAL HOLE THAT A REFEREE WILL FIND IMMEDIATELY. The frozen protocol (section 2, L5 row) promises 'DeepONet, FNO, WNO, DeepOKAN, matched budget'. l5_rerun.log shows only deeponet and deepokan were ever run. Both of the architectures actually executed are linear-reconstruction methods, which is exactly the class Lanthaler et al. PROVE will fail on advection-dominated problems. We then report their failure as evidence about operator learning in general. That inference does not hold, and the protocol's own text convicts us. Either run FNO (and one nonlinear-reconstruction method) or amend the protocol in RETRACTIONS.md and restate L5's scope as 'linear-reconstruction operator learners'.

THE PROJECT'S THEORY IS NOW ITS BIGGEST ASSET RATHER THAN A RETRACTION. RESULTS.md treats A17 as an embarrassment: the n-width was predicted to bind and it was measured inactive. Lanthaler et al. plus Heinlein & Taraz turn this into a clean, citable story: the n-width bound is a LOWER bound on a term (basis error) that is not the dominant term; the dominant term is the parameter-to-coefficient map, and that is a statistical/branch problem, not an approximation-theory problem. Our data measures the split (basis error falls 28.7x, coefficient error flat at 0.051) on an engineering system, which neither cited paper does. That is a publishable refinement, not a retraction.

THE TWO-WAVE STRUCTURE IS NOT A DISCOVERY, IT IS A DERIVATION. RESULTS.md calls the two-wave breakthrough 'KEY PHYSICS FINDING'. For an isotherm with an inflection point, classical equilibrium chromatography theory (Rhee-Aris-Amundson; Helfferich & Klein) predicts a combined wave: a self-sharpening shock on the favourable branch plus a spreading simple wave on the unfavourable branch. Presenting this as a finding invites an easy and damaging referee comment. Presented instead as 'our solver reproduces the classical combined-wave structure, and we then measure that its 40-fold separation is what breaks single-frame reduction', it becomes a strength: verification of the reference AND the motivation for the two-shift warp, in one move.

L7's CLASSICAL CONTROL IS TOO WEAK FOR THE PHYSICS WE CHOSE. We beat Klinkenberg (linear isotherm), constant-pattern (non-spreading favourable front) and equilibrium-shock (infinitely fast kinetics) by 3.2x, and then correctly note that all three assume physics that is not present. That is close to a strawman by our own protocol's trap #3. The correct classical control for an inflected isotherm is the equilibrium combined-wave solution (shock + simple wave, from the isotherm's own inflection), not a single shock. If learning still wins against THAT, L7 becomes a much stronger result.

THE MATERIAL-COUNT LEARNING CURVE PARTIALLY CONTRADICTS L1 AND THE LITERATURE SIDES WITH THE LEARNING CURVE. learning_curve.log shows 1.82x improvement (0.0929 -> 0.0509) going from 12 to 48 training materials, unsaturated. L1 said 'more data is eliminated'. Those are compatible only because L1 varied conditions-per-material, not materials. Every transfer-learning result in materials ML says the material axis is the one that matters. This must be stated as a scoped correction to L1 IN THE PAPER, not buried, or a referee who notices the log will treat the whole ladder as unreliable. The 240-material scale-up dataset is therefore not optional polish; it is the fix for the ladder's weakest verdict.

OUR OWN 'STRONGEST CONFIGURATION' RULE HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED TO DEEPONET. l5_fill2.log shows lr=3e-3 (above the previous grid top) reaching ~0.0275 at p=128, better than the recorded 0.0296 — the grid did not bracket DeepONet's optimum either, not just DeepOKAN's. Combined with the missing two-step training (Lee & Shin 2023) and missing POD-DeepONet, our DeepONet is demonstrably not at its strongest. This is trap #3 for the fifth time and it is the kind of thing that, once found, costs a paper its credibility on everything else.

THE ADSORPTION COMMUNITY WILL JUDGE US ON A DIFFERENT AXIS THAN THE ML COMMUNITY. For IECR/Sep.Purif.Technol./Chem.Eng.Sci., the questions are: does it predict a KPI an engineer uses (breakthrough time, working capacity, energy), is it validated against an experiment, and does it beat the adsorbent-agnostic ANN. For JCP/CMAME/npj Comp.Mater., the questions are: is the split honest, is the floor measured, is the comparison matched, is the negative result airtight. Our ladder answers the second set superbly and the first set barely. The venue decision should be made deliberately, and the framing rewritten to match — trying to satisfy both without experimental data is how papers get desk-rejected twice.

01_INTRODUCTION.md AND 02_METHODOLOGY_JUSTIFICATION.md ARE NOW ACTIVE LIABILITIES. They assert that data-driven models suffer 'catastrophic error explosions' (retracted as A15), that PIKAN/DeepOKAN are 'the optimal mathematical architecture' (refuted by our own L3 and L5), that we present 'the first unified architecture', and that MLP/XGBoost/RF are included 'strictly as strawman baselines' — while our results show XGBoost is the best arm in L1 and beats every KAN. If any of that text survives into a submission it contradicts our own data in the same PDF. They should be deleted and rewritten from RESULTS.md, not edited.
risks_to_our_claims: 'You tested only linear-reconstruction operators and concluded operators do not help.' Lanthaler et al. (arXiv:2210.01074) prove DeepONet and POD+regressor are the wrong tools for advection-dominated problems and that FNO escapes the bound. Our own frozen protocol lists FNO and WNO in L5; the logs show neither was run. This is the single most likely reason for rejection and it is documented in our own repository.

'Your main mechanism was published six months before you.' Heinlein & Taraz (arXiv:2602.21910, Feb 2026) already report that DeepONet error is branch-dominated at large internal dimension with spectral bias across modes — qualitatively identical to our L5 bottleneck analysis, which CONTINUE_HERE.md calls the strongest result in the project.

'Your positive result is shifted POD with two frames.' sPOD (Reiss et al. 2015/2018) exists precisely for 'multiple transport phenomena', robust multi-transport sPOD exists (Krah et al. 2024/25), and neural sPOD (Zorawski et al. 2024) already learns the transports jointly with the fields — which is the exact obstruction we report as open ('the entire 2.5x is consumed by front-location error'). If we present the two-wave warp as novel, a ROM referee will reject on prior art; if we present it as a domain instantiation with a measured n-width collapse, it stands.

'Your two-wave physics is textbook.' An inflected (Type IV/V) isotherm producing shock + spreading simple wave is classical equilibrium chromatography theory. Calling it a key finding is an easy target, and it simultaneously undermines L7, where we only used a single-shock equilibrium baseline.

'Your DeepONet was undertrained / under-tuned, so the flat-in-p null is an artifact.' l5_fill2.log already shows a better DeepONet outside the recorded grid (lr=3e-3, ~0.0275 at p=128). Two-step trunk-then-branch training (Lee & Shin 2023) and POD-DeepONet (Lu et al. 2022) are standard stronger configurations we never ran. Our own trap #3 says this invalidates the margin.

'Your L1 verdict is contradicted by your own learning curve.' 1.82x and unsaturated over 12->48 training materials directly weakens 'more data is eliminated'. The scale-up dataset that would settle it is incomplete (~1457 of 4080 files, no manifest).

'You never compared against the field's own baseline.' Pai et al.'s adsorbent-agnostic ANN (IECR 2020, ~59 citations, experimentally validated 2022) is the established material-spanning surrogate in adsorption. It is absent from our manuscript. Similarly absent: GP regression and greedy kernel methods, which are the published state of the art for breakthrough-curve prediction in the reactive-porous-media literature.

'The reference solution is a 1-D model with placeholder parameters and no experiment.' We verify the solver against analytic solutions OF ITS OWN MODEL, every MOF-303 parameter is an uncited literature-range placeholder (A4), and there is no experimental validation and no COF despite the title. arXiv:2502.05029 defends the 1-D model class and should be cited, but it does not substitute for a digitised published breakthrough curve.

'Your KAN result contradicts the literature.' Recent arXiv KAN-vs-MLP PDE benchmarks report KAN winning almost uniformly (I enumerated ~19; essentially all positive). Our L3 is against that tide. It is defensible — Shukla et al. CMAME 2024 is the counter-anchor, and our result is matched-parameter with a hyperparameter audit — but the rebuttal must be written in advance, in the paper, not left to review.

'Two of your manuscript drafts contradict your results.' 01_INTRODUCTION.md and 02_METHODOLOGY_JUSTIFICATION.md still claim PIKAN/DeepOKAN optimality, catastrophic ML failure, and strawman tree baselines — all now refuted by our own rungs.

UNVERIFIED BUT POTENTIALLY FATAL TO THE WARP SECTION: an SSRN 2026 preprint titled 'Scale-up prediction of breakthrough curves via shape-timescale decomposition in a hybrid deep learning framework' (10.2139/ssrn.6874257). I could not retrieve it (403) and cannot say what it contains. The title describes shape/timescale separation for breakthrough curves. It must be read before the warp section is written.

concrete_actions.action: Run FNO on the L5 encoding at matched ~200k parameters, matched 8000 steps, 3 seeds, across p / mode counts, on the same novel-material split. Add one nonlinear-reconstruction arm alongside it — NOMAD (arXiv:2206.03551, code public) or shift-DeepONet (arXiv:2210.01074).
concrete_actions.rationale: The protocol promised FNO and WNO and neither was run; the two arms that WERE run are exactly the class Lanthaler et al. prove must fail. Without this, L5's conclusion is not supported by L5's evidence, and the gap is documented in our own frozen protocol. This is also the highest-information experiment left: if FNO/NOMAD are also flat, the coefficient-map claim becomes very strong and the paper gets a theorem-plus-measurement structure; if they are not, we learn it before a referee does.

concrete_actions.action: Read Ceccanti et al. (arXiv:2601.09491), Meng et al. (10.1021/acs.iecr.5c04676), Pai et al. (10.1021/acs.iecr.0c02339) and Heinlein & Taraz (arXiv:2602.21910) in full, then write a Related Work section that states for each: what they predict, what they split on, and what we do differently. Retrieve the SSRN shape-timescale preprint (10.2139/ssrn.6874257) before writing the warp section.
concrete_actions.rationale: Four of these were published in the last eight months and each covers ground the manuscript currently implies is open. The 'no one has done DeepONet for adsorption columns' and 'we discovered the coefficient-map bottleneck' framings are both now false. Establishing the split distinction (conditions vs materials) in writing is what preserves our novelty claim.

concrete_actions.action: Delete 01_INTRODUCTION.md and 02_METHODOLOGY_JUSTIFICATION.md and rewrite from RESULTS.md, dropping every claim listed in RETRACTIONS.md (catastrophic extrapolation failure, PIKAN/DeepOKAN optimality, 'strawman' tree baselines, 'first unified architecture', COF, MOF-303 by name).
concrete_actions.rationale: These drafts assert the opposite of what L1, L3, L5 and L4b measured. Their survival into a submission would put self-contradiction inside a single PDF and destroy the credibility that RETRACTIONS.md was built to earn.

concrete_actions.action: Re-run DeepONet at its true optimum: extend the lr grid upward past 3e-3 until it turns over, and add two stronger standard configurations — POD-DeepONet (fixed POD trunk, learn only the coefficient map; Lu et al. CMAME 2022) and two-step trunk-then-branch training with Gram-Schmidt (Lee & Shin, arXiv:2309.01020). Report all at matched budget and 3 seeds.
concrete_actions.rationale: l5_fill2.log already shows the recorded grid did not bracket the optimum. POD-DeepONet is the ideal instrument for our own thesis: it isolates the coefficient map by construction, so if it also sits at ~0.028-0.051 the bottleneck claim is proven in the field's own currency rather than inferred. This closes trap #3 before review.

concrete_actions.action: Reposition the two-wave warp inside the registration/sPOD literature: cite Reiss et al. 2018, Taddei 2019, Nair & Balajewicz 2017, Mojgani & Balajewicz 2017, Krah et al. 2024/25; benchmark our warp against a multi-transport sPOD decomposition of the same 691 training fields.
concrete_actions.rationale: The idea of multiple co-moving frames is a decade old. Claiming it as new invites a prior-art rejection from any ROM reviewer. Benchmarking against sPOD converts the risk into a result: either our two-landmark physical warp beats a general-purpose method (a real contribution) or sPOD does better and we have found a stronger method for the paper's one positive finding.

concrete_actions.action: Replace the two-stage warp pipeline (fit shifts, then POD, then regress coefficients) with an end-to-end model that learns the front locations and the warped-frame shape jointly, following neural sPOD (Zorawski et al., arXiv:2407.17539) and the parametric sPOD-deep-learning ROM (Burela et al., arXiv:2304.14872).
concrete_actions.rationale: Our own measurement says the residual 2.17x headroom is entirely in front-location error, and that shifts fitted against a proxy objective are not fitted against the reconstruction error they actually control. This is the specific published remedy for the specific obstruction we identified, and it is the only realistic route to a positive result strong enough to headline the paper.

concrete_actions.action: Reframe the two-wave breakthrough as reproduction of the classical combined-wave (shock plus spreading simple wave) for an inflected isotherm, and add the corresponding equilibrium combined-wave solution as the strong classical control in L7, replacing single-shock equilibrium theory.
concrete_actions.rationale: Presenting textbook behaviour as a discovery is an unforced error, and the weak classical baseline makes L7's 3.2x margin look manufactured under our own 'strongest competitor' rule. Beating the correct combined-wave solution would make L7 genuinely load-bearing; losing to it would be an even more interesting result.

concrete_actions.action: Finish the 240-material scale-up dataset (data/parametric_scale, ~1457/4080 files, no manifest) and extend the material-count learning curve past 48. Then publish a scoped correction to L1 in the paper: 'more conditions per material is eliminated; more MATERIALS is not.'
concrete_actions.rationale: The learning curve contradicts the L1 verdict on the axis that matters most for transfer, and it is currently only in a log file. Publishing the ladder with a verdict our own unreported data undermines is the worst available outcome; publishing the correction ourselves is the best, and is exactly the behaviour the retraction ledger is meant to demonstrate.

concrete_actions.action: Add a Gaussian-process baseline and a greedy-kernel baseline on the exit-curve task, following the reactive-porous-media breakthrough-curve benchmark line (arXiv:2204.11719, 2301.04998, 2405.19170), and add an 'adsorbent-agnostic ANN' arm in the style of Pai et al. as the domain reference point.
concrete_actions.rationale: L1/L2 eliminate 'more data' and 'more capacity' using only trees and MLPs. Kernel methods and GPs are the published state of the art for this exact task and are the obvious counterexample a numerical-analysis referee raises. The GP also supplies calibrated uncertainty on the novel-material split, which no current arm provides.

concrete_actions.action: Digitise one published experimental water (or CO2) breakthrough curve on a named MOF, refit the isotherm to a published measured water isotherm, and validate the SOLVER against it — reporting solver-vs-experiment and surrogate-vs-solver as two separate lines of the error budget. Cite arXiv:2502.05029 to defend the 1-D model class and Pai et al. 2022 as precedent for experimental closure.
concrete_actions.rationale: Closes open items 1 and 2 simultaneously, retires retraction A4, and is explicitly the item CONTINUE_HERE.md says 'would change the venue tier'. Without it the paper cannot claim a named material and cannot reach the top tier regardless of methodological quality.

concrete_actions.action: Re-run L6 (H1) on a dataset with k_LDF extended down to Damköhler ~1-50, and parameterise the presentation by (Da, Pe) so it is directly comparable to the published breakthrough-ML benchmarks that use those groups.
concrete_actions.rationale: Our own identifiability study explains H1's failure as near-degeneracy at median Da 626, and the protocol pre-declares this re-test. Either outcome is publishable, and reporting in (Da, Pe) makes our numbers legible to the porous-media ML community whose benchmarks already use that axis.

concrete_actions.action: Choose the venue before rewriting, and write to it: methods venue (JCP/CMAME/npj Comp. Mater.) leading with the falsification ladder, the material-transfer split and the n-width floor; or domain venue (IECR / Sep. Purif. Technol. / Chem. Eng. Sci.) leading with breakthrough-time and working-capacity error against the adsorbent-agnostic ANN. Delete kaggle_run/ either way.
concrete_actions.rationale: The two audiences grade on disjoint criteria and the current draft satisfies neither fully. Without experimental data the domain framing is weak; with the FNO gap unclosed the methods framing is attackable. Fixing the two critical actions above makes the methods venue reachable; the experimental curve makes the domain venue strong.

lens: Numerical methods and verification standards for fixed-bed adsorption column simulation — is the ground truth defensible?
state_of_the_art:
Short answer: your solver is *above* the community norm on numerics and *below* the norm on two specific things — the coupled non-isothermal verification, and the physical closure of the thermal/kinetic parameters. And one naming error (calling the isotherm "Do–Do") is a referee grenade.

(1) FIRST-ORDER UPWIND IS NOT THE PROBLEM, AND IS EASY TO DEFEND. The reference open-source breakthrough code in this field — RUPTURA (Sharma et al., Mol. Simul. 2023, from the Vlugt/Calero/Dubbeldam/Snurr orbit, the code the MOF community actually cites) — uses first-order upwind advection with SSP-RK3 and has NO energy balance at all. I read `src/breakthrough.cpp` directly to confirm both. Your solver is strictly more complete than the field's own reference implementation: implicit BDF with an analytic Jacobian sparsity pattern, plus a coupled energy equation. Meanwhile the higher-order literature (Medi & Amanullah 2010 IECR; Javeed/Qamar/Seidel-Morgenstern/Warnecke 2011 CACE; Haghpanah et al. 2013 IECR; Breuer et al. 2023 CACE for DG-SEM in CADET) argues for TVD/WENO/DG on *cost* grounds — same accuracy at 10–50× fewer cells — not because upwind is wrong. Nobody in this literature claims upwind at a resolved grid is invalid.

The decisive defense, which you are not currently making and which I computed from your own frozen configuration: your first-order numerical dispersion is bounded, analytically and over the *entire* parameter space, at a fixed small fraction of the physical dispersion. Because you set D_L by the Ruthven correlation D_L = 0.7·D_m + 0.5·d_p·u, the ratio D_num/D_L = (u·Δz/2)/(0.7D_m + 0.5 d_p u) ≤ Δz/d_p = 5×10⁻⁵/2×10⁻³ = **2.5%**, for every velocity, forever. Evaluated at the three corners of your CONDITION_SPACE (v = 0.03/eps = 0.48; v = 0.10/eps = 0.40; v = 0.30/eps = 0.30) it is 1.95%, 2.34%, 2.46%. The cell Péclet number u·Δz/D_L is 0.039, 0.047, 0.049 — bounded above by Δz/(0.5 d_p) = 0.05, i.e. **40× below** the Pe_cell = 2 threshold at which upwind's artificial diffusion starts to matter. The energy equation is the same story: α_T = k_z/C_term = 1.39×10⁻⁷ m²/s, u_thermal = 1.67×10⁻⁴ m/s, so Pe_cell,T = 0.06 and D_num,T/α_T = 3.0%. This is a two-line proof that upwind at N_z = 2000 is a *resolved* calculation, not a shock-capturing gamble. It is much stronger than "error halves as N_z doubles," and it should be in the paper. State it as: "the scheme's equivalent dispersion inflates D_L by at most 2.5% and α_T by 3.0% anywhere in the sampled space; the discretisation is diffusion-resolved (Pe_cell < 0.05), so the fronts in this dataset are physically, not numerically, broadened."

(2) WHAT A CES/AIChE J/SEPPUR REFEREE ACTUALLY EXPECTS. There is no formal V&V standard in this field the way ASME V&V 20 / Roache's GCI operate in CFD, and adsorption papers are notoriously lax — most validate against experiment and never verify the code. But a *numerics-forward* paper (which yours is, since the solver IS the dataset) gets held to the CFD bar. The expected checklist is: (a) analytic limits — the canonical set is Danckwerts/Brenner (1962) for the finite-bed dispersed plug-flow tracer, Klinkenberg (1948) for the LDF asymptote, Anzelius/Schumann (1929) for the thermal-exchange J-function, Rosen (1952) for intraparticle diffusion, and Hall/Eagleton/Acrivos/Vermeulen (1966) for the constant-pattern limit with a favourable isotherm; (b) an *observed order of accuracy* from ≥3 grids with Richardson extrapolation and a GCI, per Roache; (c) global conservation closure for **every** conserved quantity; (d) ideally MMS (Roache 2002) for the full coupled operator. You have (a) partially and (c) for mass only. You have clean first-order behaviour but you never report the fitted observed order p or a GCI — that is a five-minute addition that converts "error halves" into a number a referee recognises.

(3) THE REAL HOLE: EVERY L0 CHECK DECOUPLES THE PHYSICS. Read `verify_solver.py` honestly — the four benchmarks are (i) inert tracer, adsorption off; (ii) *linear* isotherm retarded front; (iii) thermal wave with **adsorption off**; (iv) LDF with a linear isotherm. Not one of them exercises the production regime: nonlinear Type V equilibrium, heat of adsorption feeding back into b(T), and the two-wave structure simultaneously. The coupling term heat_factor·dq/dt → q*(c,T) is the single most error-prone line in the solver and it is verified by **nothing**. This is the objection I would raise as a referee, and it is the one that would actually stick. It is also fixable: Qamar and co-workers published closed-form solutions for *linearised coupled* non-isothermal column models with an energy balance (Uche/Qamar/Seidel-Morgenstern, Adsorption 25:1487, 2019; Ahmad/Qamar/Seidel-Morgenstern, JLCRT 42:436, 2019). Linearise your isotherm about a reference state, retain the adsorption-heat source, and you have a fifth benchmark that tests the coupling itself. Separately, the equilibrium (Da → ∞) limit gives you the exact shock velocity from the jump condition u_sh = v/(ε + (1−ε)ρ_p Δq/Δc) with **no** fitting — that is a free, exact test of the *nonlinear* isotherm in the production regime, and you already have the classical machinery for it in L7 (you are using Klinkenberg/constant-pattern/equilibrium-shock as ML *baselines*; they should also be doing duty as *verification*).

(4) ENERGY BALANCE. You report global mass closure of 0.050% and no energy closure at all. That asymmetry will be noticed immediately in a paper whose headline physics is a *thermal* wave riding ahead of the mass front. Add d/dt ∫[C_term·T]dz = v ρ_g C_pg (T_in − T_exit) + (1−ε)ρ_p(−ΔH)∫dq/dt dz − (4h_w/D_in)∫(T−T_w)dz and report the residual as a percentage. Your Danckwerts fix in `laplacian()` (zero dispersive flux at the inlet face) makes the mass telescoping exact; check that the *same* treatment on the T equation makes the energy sum telescope too — if it doesn't, you have a bug you haven't found.

(5) TWO PHYSICAL PARAMETERS ARE HARD-CODED WHERE THEY SHOULD BE CORRELATED, AND ONE OF THEM IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT WITH THE OTHER. You correlate D_L to d_p and v (good — you explicitly say this is "defensible to a referee"), but `k_z = 0.10 W/m/K` is a constant in `AdsorptionPhysicsConfig` and never varies with velocity. The standard closure is λ_ax = λ_bed⁰ + 0.5·ρ_g·c_pg·v·d_p (Pe_h,ax → 2, Wakao & Kaguei / Vortmeyer). The flow term alone is 0.036, 0.120, 0.360 W/m/K at v = 0.03, 0.10, 0.30 — so at the top of your velocity range you are under-dispersing heat by ~3.6× *and* the static-bed conductivity (0.1–0.3 W/m/K for a packed MOF) is missing entirely. A referee who correlates D_L and not k_z will be asked why. Same for `h_w = 10 W/m²/K`, a bare constant where the literature uses a wall-Nusselt correlation, and where Born et al. (CES 276:118810, 2023) show experimentally that an uninsulated lab column loses ~20% of the thermal signal versus an insulated one, and that the column *wall thermal mass* — absent from your energy balance — is a first-order effect at lab scale.

(6) THE k_LDF PROBLEM IS BIGGER THAN YOUR OPEN-ITEM LIST SAYS, AND IT REACHES INTO L6. Two separate defects. (a) *Internal inconsistency*: D_L is computed from d_p = 2 mm, but k_LDF is sampled independently over (0.002, 0.05) s⁻¹. For a 2 mm pellet under macropore control, k = 15·D_eff/R_p² with D_eff ~ 10⁻⁶ m²/s gives k ≈ 15 s⁻¹ — 300–7500× your sampled range. Your sampled k_LDF implies D_eff ≈ 3×10⁻⁹ m²/s, which is crystallite/micropore-controlled, i.e. R in the LDF formula is a crystal radius, not the pellet radius that sets D_L. That is defensible physics *if you say so*; as written the two transport resistances describe two different particles. (b) *The Damköhler consequence, which I think you have not connected*: at your reported Da = 155–3885 the column is at or near local equilibrium, where the front width is dispersion-controlled and the solution's sensitivity to k_LDF scales like 1/N_TU. **This is very likely the physical cause of your L6 headline** — "k_LDF is unrecoverable from observable descriptors (R² = −0.61)". It may not be an identifiability statement about surrogates at all; it may be a statement that you sampled a regime in which k_LDF barely affects the observable. Before publishing L6 as a general finding, regenerate a slice with Da ~ 1–50 and re-run the identification. If k_LDF becomes recoverable there, L6's claim must be re-scoped to "near-equilibrium columns" — a much narrower but *honest* and still interesting result. If it stays unrecoverable, L6 gets dramatically stronger because you have ruled out the obvious confound. Either way this is the highest-leverage experiment in this lens.

(7) LDF VS PORE/SURFACE DIFFUSION FOR TYPE V WATER — YES, THERE IS LITERATURE, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. The defense of LDF is Sircar & Hufton (Adsorption 6:137, 2000): particle-level kinetic detail is repeatedly averaged away in column breakthrough, so LDF and Fickian diffusion give near-identical *breakthrough* curves even when their *uptake* curves differ substantially. Cite this — it is the standard answer and it is specifically about column dynamics. The attack is: (i) Do & Rice (AIChE J 32:149, 1986) show the parabolic-profile assumption underlying k = 15D/R² breaks for strongly nonlinear isotherms; (ii) Georgiou & Kupiec (Chem. Eng. J. 92:185, 2003) and Georgiou (CES 59:3591, 2004) build explicit nonlinear-driving-force corrections precisely because the constant-k LDF has large errors for nonlinear isotherm systems, worst as fractional uptake → 1 — which is exactly the cooperative-shock branch of your Type V curve; (iii) most damaging and most recent, Ma et al. (Nano Lett. 25:5778, 2025) show for water in MOFs specifically that free diffusion / LDF holds at low RH, but *above the step* water condenses into clusters and needs a two-concentration framework — i.e. a single constant k_LDF is exactly wrong across the step you are building your whole physics story on. A referee who works on MOF water will know this paper. Pre-empt it: state the LDF assumption, cite Sircar & Hufton for why breakthrough is forgiving, cite Ma et al. as the acknowledged limitation, and — ideally — run a handful of pore-diffusion or Georgiou-NLDF spot-checks to bound the error.

(8) THE ISOTHERM NAME IS WRONG, AND THIS ONE IS SERIOUS. Your `isotherm.py` implements q = q_max[f_H·b_H c/(1+b_H c) + (1−f_H)(b_C c)^n/(1+(b_C c)^n)]. That is a **dual-site Langmuir–Freundlich (DSLF) / Langmuir + Sips-Hill** equation. It is *not* the Do–Do model. Do & Do (Carbon 38:767, 2000) is a cluster-formation model in *relative pressure*: water hydrogen-bonds onto surface functional groups, clusters grow to a critical size (n ≈ 5 molecules), and only then does micropore filling begin; it has 5–6 parameters (q_sat, f, K_f, K_μ, cluster size n, m) and has no term of your form. Every occurrence of "Do–Do" in `isotherm.py`, `03_LADDER_PROTOCOL.md`, `RESULTS.md`, and the manuscript drafts is a misattribution. Any referee from the water-adsorption community catches this in the first ten seconds and it poisons their read of everything else. The fix costs an hour and *strengthens* the paper: DSLF is thoroughly standard for MOFs (RUPTURA ships Langmuir-Freundlich as one of its 13 models), and your actual argument — that a bare Hill/Sips term violates Henry's law (q ~ c^n, dq/dc → 0 at the origin) and that adding a Henry-carrying Langmuir site restores the linear limit while preserving the step — is a *good* argument that stands entirely on its own without a borrowed name.

(9) WOULD A REFEREE OBJECT TO THE ISOTHERM ITSELF? Under its correct name, no — DSLF is mainstream. The competitors a 2026 MOF-water referee would name are: Sun & Chakraborty's Fermi–Dirac-derived isotherm (Chakraborty & Sun, Appl. Therm. Eng. 72:190, 2014), which is the model most often used for S-shaped MOF water isotherms in the adsorption-cooling/AWH community; Dubinin–Astakhov, widely used for Type V MOF water; GAB; and the "universal isotherm" family from Ng and co-workers. The Shih & Lin JACS review (147:34791, 2025) is the current canonical reference for MOF water isotherm characteristics and structure–property relationships and should be cited. One substantive physical objection remains regardless of name: because both your sites carry the *same* ΔH, your isosteric heat is exactly −ΔH at every loading by construction. Real Type V water systems do not behave that way — q_st falls from ~55–60 kJ/mol at low loading toward the enthalpy of vaporisation (~44 kJ/mol) inside the pore-filling step. You currently sell the constant q_st as a feature ("Clausius–Clapeyron satisfied by construction"); a referee will read it as a limitation. Say both.

(10) MINOR BUT CHECKABLE.
