papers.what_it_shows: Data-based surrogates predicting breakthrough curves from 3-D pore-scale geometry under SCARCE data with high input and output dimension. Standard ML fails in that regime; greedy kernel approximation - specifically vectorial kernel orthogonal greedy approximation (VKOGA) with a data-adapted two-layer kernel - yields excellent predictors from morphological descriptors or PCA of voxel data.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Same target quantity as our L7/exit-curve rung, from a top MOR group (Haasdonk). Two implications: (a) it is a must-cite in our related work or our domain novelty looks unexamined; (b) VKOGA with a data-adapted kernel is a concrete, published-in-our-domain alternative to HistGradientBoosting for our warp regression, and it is designed for exactly our regime (few materials, high-dimensional descriptors).

papers.citation: Daria Fokina, Oleg Iliev, Pavel Toktaliev, Ivan Oseledets, Felix Schindler, "On the Performance of Machine Learning Methods for Breakthrough Curve Prediction"
papers.what_it_shows: Systematic comparison of ML methods predicting breakthrough curves from parameters (Damkoehler and Peclet numbers) in 1-D and 3-D reactive porous media.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Prior work that already benchmarks ML surrogates for breakthrough curves parameterised by Damkoehler number. Directly relevant to open item 6 (our Da range 155-3885 under-samples the informative Da ~ 1-50 regime): this paper tells us what parameterisation the community expects to see swept, and it is an obvious comparison point.

papers.citation: Joubine Aghili, Hassan Ballout, Yvon Maday, Christophe Prud'homme, "Nonlinear compressive reduced basis approximation: when Taylor meets Kolmogorov"
papers.what_it_shows: Argues that when the Kolmogorov width decays slowly the right complexity measure is the GELFAND width and its sensing number; analyses splitting the N coordinates into n free and n-bar dependent variables (the latter nonlinear functions of the former), proves n = p (the parameter dimension) is locally optimal, and argues that quadratic maps are locally justified but insufficient over wide parameter ranges, motivating more expressive learned maps.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Gives a rigorous reason why our latent dimension should scale with the PARAMETER dimension p rather than with the n-width - which is a precise theoretical explanation for our observation that DeepONet is flat in p and behaves like a 4-mode reconstruction. Also predicts, correctly for us, that a quadratic/local map is not enough across wide ranges. Excellent framing citation for the discussion section.

papers.citation: Jiajia Yu, Jingwei Hu, Fengyan Li, Shanyin Tong, Yunan Yang, Zhaiming Shen, "Structure-Preserving Reduced-Order Modeling via Low-Rank Transport Signatures"
papers.what_it_shows: Represents each density by the Kantorovich potential transporting a fixed reference to the target, maps potentials to 'transport signatures' via a weighted Laplacian, builds a low-rank skeleton by maximal-volume selection, and learns the parameter-to-coefficient map with a neural network. Proves a mean-squared Wasserstein error bound separating low-rank, discretisation, sampling and LEARNING errors.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Note the error decomposition: they separate the representation error from the LEARNING error of the parameter-to-coefficient map. That is precisely our oracle-versus-predicted split, done rigorously and published in 2026. Our 'payoff curve' contribution is therefore adjacent to an existing rigorous result - cite it, and position our contribution as the empirical, measured version for a physical system rather than as a new idea.

papers.citation: Tianyu Jin, Zhichao Peng, Yang Xiang, "Adaptive and hybrid reduced order models to mitigate Kolmogorov barrier in a multiscale kinetic transport equation"
papers.what_it_shows: Goal-oriented adaptive time partitioning giving a PIECEWISE-LINEAR ROM, plus a hybrid that applies an autoencoder-based nonlinear ROM only on the time intervals adaptively identified as hardest.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: A cheap alternative philosophy we have not tested: instead of warping, PARTITION. Given that our two-wave separation varies 40x, partitioning the time axis per sample is a plausible and much simpler competitor to the warp, and a referee could reasonably suggest it. Testing it costs little and pre-empts the question.

papers.citation: Nicolas Cagniart, Yvon Maday, Benjamin Stamm, "Model Order Reduction for Problems with Large Convection Effects", in Contributions to Partial Differential Equations and Applications, Springer
papers.what_it_shows: Introduces a 'preconditioning'/calibration step: apply smooth invertible mappings (e.g. translations F_eta(x) = x - eta) to the snapshots before linear compression, to counter the slowly decaying n-width in convection-dominated problems. (Details from search results and the HAL landing page; I did not fetch the full text.)
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The standard citation for 'calibrate the snapshots before you compress'. It is single-shift, so it is another member of the family our single-front experiment refutes, and it is the term ('calibration') that Sarna et al. use. Include it in the family list.

papers.citation: Harshith Gowrachari, Giovanni Stabile et al., "Model Reduction for Transport-Dominated Problems via Cross-Correlation Based Snapshot Registration", Springer chapter (DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-11527-0_10)
papers.what_it_shows: Uses cross-correlation-based snapshot registration to accelerate n-width decay so that linear approximation methods become efficient. (Seen in search results only; abstract not fetched.)
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Cross-correlation registration is the cheapest possible automatic alignment and would be a near-zero-cost sanity baseline against our hand-designed warp. Verify the full reference before citing.

state_of_the_art: As of 2026 the field is consolidated and has an authoritative survey (Hesthaven, Peherstorfer & Unger, Acta Numerica 35, 2026; arXiv:2602.01397). Four families of remedy exist. (1) ADDITIVE multi-transport decompositions: sPOD (Reiss et al. 2015/2018) and transport reversal (Rim, Moe & LeVeque 2017) write the field as a SUM of co-moving profiles, one per wave speed; the current best version is robust sPOD via proximal/nuclear-norm optimisation (Krah et al., arXiv:2403.04313, 2024/25), with neural automation (Zorawski et al. 2024) and parametric neural forecasting (Burela, Krah & Reiss, Adv. Comput. Math. 2025). (2) COMPOSITIONAL registration/calibration: freeze a group action (Ohlberger & Rave 2013; Cagniart, Maday & Stamm 2019), or compute a general parameter-dependent diffeomorphism by variational registration (Taddei, SISC 2020, arXiv:1906.11008), extended to space-time for 1-D hyperbolic PDEs (Taddei & Zhang, M2AN 55:99-130, 2021), to spatio-parameter adaptivity (Barral, Taddei & Tifouti, JCP 499:112727, 2024), to convex displacement interpolation with landmark point clouds (Cucchiara, Iollo, Taddei & Telib, JCP 2024, arXiv:2310.04290), and, as of January 2026, to parametric vector flows in bounded domains (Labatut et al., arXiv:2601.22712). Purely data-driven variants use optimal transport (Blickhan, SISC 2024) or monotone landmark matching (Sarna, Giesselmann & Benner, FEAD 230:104065, 2024). (3) NONLINEAR DECODERS: convolutional-autoencoder manifold ROM (Lee & Carlberg, JCP 404, 2020), quadratic approximation manifolds giving n2 ~ sqrt(n1) (Barnett & Farhat, JCP 2022), Neural Implicit Flow (Pan, Brunton & Kutz, JMLR 24, 2023), NOMAD (Seidman et al., NeurIPS 2022), and Front Transport Reduction (Krah et al., J. Sci. Comput. 96, 2023). (4) OPTIMAL-TRANSPORT / metric-space ROM: Wasserstein barycentres and tangent spaces for 1-D conservative PDEs (Ehrlacher, Lombardi, Mula & Vialard, M2AN 54, 2020), extended in 2026 to low-rank transport signatures with proven error decompositions (arXiv:2607.01696). On the THEORY side, Arbes, Greif & Urban (arXiv:2305.00066) give sharp n-width rates c_r N^{-r} tied to Sobolev regularity H^{r-eps}, and Lanthaler, Molinaro, Hadorn & Mishra (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.01074) prove that ANY operator-learning architecture with a linear reconstruction step (DeepONet, PCA-Net) has expected squared L2 error bounded below by C/p, while nonlinear-reconstruction architectures (FNO, shift-DeepONet) escape it. On PREDICTING the registration - our bottleneck - the state of the art is: POD of sorted landmark point clouds followed by cross-validated Gaussian-kernel RBF regression (CDI, Cucchiara et al. 2024, section 2.3); ShiftNet MLPs trained on the RECONSTRUCTION loss rather than a warp-fitting loss (NNsPOD-ROM, Gowrachari et al., Computers & Fluids 2025, arXiv:2407.18419); registration autoencoders whose objective is the n-width of the mapped data (Mojgani & Balajewicz, arXiv:2006.15655); EM-based joint point-cloud matching and map identification (Labatut et al. 2026); greedy kernel VKOGA for scarce-data breakthrough-curve prediction specifically (Herkert et al., arXiv:2405.19170); and, from functional data analysis, SRVF / Fisher-Rao coordinates in which every regression output is automatically a valid monotone warp (Srivastava et al., arXiv:1103.3817).
implications: The two-wave warp is NOT novel as a mathematical object, and the paper must say so first. sigma = (t - t_lo(z))/(t_hi(z) - t_lo(z)) is a two-landmark, monotone, piecewise-affine time-warp. That is textbook landmark registration in functional data analysis (Kneip & Gasser, Ann. Statist. 1992; Ramsay & Li, JRSS-B 1998), it is the monotonic feature-matching calibration of Sarna, Giesselmann & Benner (FEAD 2024) transposed from x to t, it is a special case of Taddei & Zhang's space-time registration for 1-D hyperbolic PDEs (M2AN 2021), it is a two-point instance of the sorted point clouds of Cucchiara et al. (JCP 2024), and it is exactly the coordinate scale-and-shift of shift-DeepONet (Lanthaler et al., ICLR 2023) with A = 1/(t_hi - t_lo) and gamma = -t_lo/(t_hi - t_lo). Claiming invention would be the fastest possible rejection.

What IS defensible is the MECHANISM and the negative result. Every single-transform method in the literature (freezing, Lagrangian basis, Cagniart-Maday-Stamm calibration, single-shift sPOD) applies a group action that changes front POSITION but cannot change front WIDTH. The Type V isotherm gives a fast SPREADING Henry wave and a slow SELF-SHARPENING cooperative shock whose separation varies 40x. So the dominant mode of variability here is a WIDTH, not a displacement - which is why a single shift made the n-width worse (31 -> 102 modes) while a two-parameter warp collapsed it (31 -> 13). That is a clean, physical, publishable statement about which system class defeats which method, and it is what the reader should remember.

The single-front refutation is CONFIRMATORY, not novel. Reiss et al. said in 2015 that one shift is insufficient when multiple transport velocities are present; that is the founding premise of sPOD. Our contribution is that we MEASURED the cost of ignoring it in a system where it had not been quantified, including the decisive oracle test (handed the exact front trajectory for free, the co-moving frame still loses: 0.0534 vs 0.0510). The oracle control is the genuinely unusual part of the experiment and should carry the framing.

Our L5 conclusion is at serious risk because DeepONet and DeepOKAN are BOTH linear-reconstruction architectures. Lanthaler et al. (ICLR 2023) prove such methods cannot efficiently approximate operators with sharp transitions. So 'operators do not help' is currently supported only for the class that theory already predicts must fail. Any competent reviewer will point at FNO, shift-DeepONet, NOMAD or a convolutional autoencoder and ask why they were not run. This is the largest single vulnerability in the ladder.

Our n-width exponent has a home in theory. Arbes, Greif & Urban prove d_n ~ c_r n^{-r} for data of Sobolev regularity H^{r-eps}. Our measured n^{-1.23} therefore reads as a measurement of front regularity (fronts smoothed by LDF kinetics and dispersion, sitting near H^1.2), not merely as a curve fit, and it explains why we do not see the classical n^{-1/2} of a true jump. This upgrades a caveated empirical claim into a principled one at the cost of two sentences.

The oracle/predicted split is our most transferable methodological idea, but it is no longer unprecedented. arXiv:2607.01696 (2026) proves an error bound separating low-rank, discretisation, sampling and LEARNING error for a transport-based ROM. Our 'payoff curve' (blend the predicted warp toward the truth and trace nRMSE: alpha = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 giving 0.0233, 0.0269, 0.0345, 0.0427, 0.0508) is the empirical instance of that decomposition, and it is genuinely rare in the registration literature - most registration ROM papers report reconstruction with the registration computed from the true snapshot, i.e. an oracle, without ever isolating what it costs to predict it. Naming and standardising this test ('registration accuracy budget') is a real, modest, defensible contribution.

The literature's stated premise about transport fields is contradicted by our data, and that is worth reporting. Nair & Balajewicz (2017/2019) justify transported-snapshot MOR by asserting that transport fields are smooth and therefore expressible with a low-order polynomial expansion. Our warp curves are smooth yet reach only R^2 = 0.895/0.919 when extrapolated to NOVEL MATERIALS. Smoothness of the registration field does not imply predictability across a materials axis. That is a sharp, specific, empirically grounded correction to a widely repeated assumption.

There is a large, unexploited physics shortcut. Equilibrium (coherence) theory for adsorption gives wave velocities in closed form from the isotherm: dispersive-wave characteristic speed from dq/dc and shock speed from the chord Delta q / Delta c, and Zhang, Shan & Seidel-Morgenstern (J. Chromatogr. A 1107:216-225, 2006) work out precisely the two-inflection-point isotherm case that our Type V dual-term Do-Do model produces. That gives an ANALYTIC prior for t_lo(z) and t_hi(z) from the isotherm parameters alone, leaving only a kinetic/dispersive correction (governed by Da and Pe) to regress. Note the irony against NNsPOD, whose selling point is not needing the advection field: we know ours analytically and are currently not using it.

Our warp-prediction pipeline has two fixable structural defects. First, it is trained on the WRONG objective: we fit t_lo and t_hi in isolation, then pay a nonlinear penalty in field error. NNsPOD-ROM's ShiftNet and Mojgani & Balajewicz's registration autoencoder both train the registration against the downstream reconstruction/n-width objective instead. Second, monotonicity and span positivity are enforced by an ad-hoc clamp (hi_pred = max(hi_pred, lo_pred + 1e-3)); the SRVF / Fisher-Rao representation of Srivastava et al. (2011) makes both automatic by construction.

Domain novelty needs qualifying. ML surrogates for breakthrough curves already exist from serious MOR groups: Fokina et al. (arXiv:2204.11719, 2022) sweep Damkoehler and Peclet, and Herkert, Buchfink, Wenzel, Haasdonk, Toktaliev & Iliev (arXiv:2405.19170, 2024) use greedy kernel VKOGA for 3-D pore-scale breakthrough curves under scarce data. Our defensible domain claim is narrower and still strong: first application of registration-based nonlinear MOR to a Type V two-wave adsorption front, and first controlled falsification of single-front alignment in that setting.
risks_to_our_claims: Novelty of the two-wave warp. A referee from the MOR or FDA community cites Kneip & Gasser (1992), Ramsay & Li (1998), Sarna-Giesselmann-Benner (FEAD 2024), Welper (2015/2019), Taddei & Zhang (M2AN 2021) or shift-DeepONet (ICLR 2023) and says: this is two-landmark monotone registration, known for thirty years. If the manuscript presents sigma as an invention, this is a desk-level rejection.

L5's design flaw. Lanthaler, Molinaro, Hadorn & Mishra prove linear-reconstruction operator learners are lower-bounded by C/p on problems with sharp transitions. We tested only DeepONet and DeepOKAN, both linear-reconstruction. 'The operator rung is eliminated' therefore overclaims: we eliminated the class the theory already condemned. Missing arms a referee will name: FNO, shift-DeepONet, NOMAD, convolutional-autoencoder manifold ROM (Lee & Carlberg), quadratic manifold (Barnett & Farhat), Neural Implicit Flow.

Headlining the oracle number. '0.0203 beats DeepONet's 0.0281' uses the ORACLE warp. Any experienced reviewer will call this a leaked-label comparison. The honest headline is 0.0508 predicted versus 0.0510 fixed frame, i.e. a tie, with a measured 2.17x of unrealised headroom. If the abstract leads with 0.0203, the paper's credibility - which is otherwise this project's greatest asset - is destroyed in one sentence.

An unbracketed baseline grid. l5_fill2.log shows DeepONet reaching ~0.0275 at lr = 3e-3, ABOVE the previous top of the learning-rate grid, better than the recorded 0.0296. A hyper-parameter search whose optimum sits on the boundary is not a search. Every 'X is eliminated' verdict that depends on that grid is contestable until the grid is extended until the optimum is interior.

No sPOD baseline. sPOD is the field-standard method for multiple transports, has public code (robust sPOD, Krah et al. 2024/25), and addresses exactly our two-wave situation with a different (additive) mechanism. Its absence is the most predictable single referee request.

The n-width exponent's scope. n^-1.23 was fitted over n = 8-64 on a 128x128 subsampled encoding of 691 training fields. Both the subsampling and the fit window affect the exponent. Arbes-Greif-Urban's sharp theory will invite scrutiny; the existing caveat in section 6d is correct but must survive into the manuscript rather than being dropped for the abstract.

The learning curve contradicts L1. In the two-wave frame, error improves 1.82x (0.0929 -> 0.0509) as training materials go 12 -> 48 and has NOT saturated. 'More data is eliminated' is therefore false on the material axis, and the scale-up dataset that would settle it (data/parametric_scale) is incomplete at roughly 1457 of 4080 runs with no manifest. Publishing L1 as an elimination while holding an unsaturated learning curve in the same repository is an integrity risk, not merely a presentational one.

Domain-novelty overreach. Herkert et al. (2024) and Fokina et al. (2022, 2023) already publish ML surrogates for breakthrough curves; Zhang, Shan & Seidel-Morgenstern (2006) already derive the two-wave structure for two-inflection-point isotherms from equilibrium theory. Claiming either the two-wave physics or ML breakthrough-curve surrogacy as new would be straightforwardly refuted.

Wasserstein methods will be raised, and we need a prepared answer. Ehrlacher-Lombardi-Mula-Vialard treat exactly 1-D transport-dominated problems. The correct response is that our c-field is a saturating breakthrough profile, not a conserved density, so Wasserstein barycentres do not apply directly - but that argument must be IN the paper, not improvised at review.

Cheaper competitors we never tested. A quadratic approximation manifold (Barnett & Farhat) needs no front tracking at all and gives n2 ~ sqrt(n1); adaptive piecewise-linear time partitioning (Jin, Peng & Xiang, arXiv:2505.08214) is a simpler answer to the same 40x separation spread. If either gets near 0.02 in the fixed frame, the warp's necessity collapses.

concrete_actions.action: Rewrite the two-wave section to CEDE the transform and CLAIM the mechanism. State in the first paragraph that sigma is a two-landmark monotone time-warp, citing Kneip & Gasser (1992), Ramsay & Li (1998), Sarna-Giesselmann-Benner (FEAD 230:104065, 2024), Welper (arXiv:1901.01322), Taddei & Zhang (M2AN 55:99-130, 2021) and shift-DeepONet (Lanthaler et al., arXiv:2210.01074). Then state the three things that ARE ours: (i) the mechanistic finding that in a Type V two-wave adsorption front the dominant variability is a WIDTH, not a displacement, so every single-group-action method is structurally incapable and measurably harmful (31 -> 102 modes); (ii) the oracle-controlled refutation of single-front alignment; (iii) the registration accuracy budget.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is the difference between a rejection on novelty and a defensible contribution. Owning the prior art converts the strongest available attack into evidence of scholarship, and the width-versus-position mechanism is a real, transferable, previously unstated criterion for when single-shift methods fail.

concrete_actions.action: Never headline the oracle number. Change every abstract-level and section-level claim to the predicted-warp figure: two-wave frame 0.0508 versus fixed frame 0.0510 (a tie), oracle 0.0233, headroom 2.17x. Present 0.0203/0.0233 only inside a clearly labelled oracle row, and state in the same sentence that it uses the true front locations.
concrete_actions.rationale: The current framing ('0.0203 beats DeepONet's 0.0281') compares an oracle against a prediction. One reviewer noticing this discredits the entire falsification-ladder methodology, which is the project's principal asset.

concrete_actions.action: Build a physics-informed warp predictor from equilibrium theory. Compute analytic wave arrival times from the isotherm: dispersive-wave characteristics from dq/dc and the self-sharpening shock from the chord Delta q / Delta c, following the two-inflection-point analysis of Zhang, Shan & Seidel-Morgenstern (J. Chromatogr. A 1107:216-225, 2006). Use these as t_lo^EQ(z), t_hi^EQ(z) and regress only the kinetic/dispersive RESIDUAL (as a function of Damkoehler and Peclet). Report R^2 against the current 0.895/0.919 and re-run the payoff curve.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is the single highest-expected-value experiment in the project. The 2.17x headroom is entirely gated on warp accuracy, the payoff curve is brutally nonlinear near alpha = 1, and we currently discard analytic information the MOR literature would give a great deal to have (NNsPOD's entire selling point is coping WITHOUT it). Even a partial success turns a tie into the paper's main result.

concrete_actions.action: Retrain the warp predictor on the DOWNSTREAM reconstruction loss instead of on warp error. Make warp2/unwarp2 differentiable, place a small network (or a differentiable parameterisation of the existing PCA-plus-regressor) in front of it, and minimise field nRMSE end-to-end - the ShiftNet objective of Gowrachari et al. (Computers & Fluids 2025, arXiv:2407.18419) and the mapped-n-width objective of Mojgani & Balajewicz (arXiv:2006.15655). Report against the identical two-stage pipeline.
concrete_actions.rationale: Our own payoff curve proves the two-stage split is the wrong objective: R^2 falling from 1.00 to 0.895 costs the error 0.0233 -> 0.0508, so warp error and field error are far from proportional. Optimising the quantity we actually care about is both the published practice and directly indicated by our own measurement.

concrete_actions.action: Add the missing operator/decoder baselines to L5 at matched encoding and budget: shift-DeepONet (the exact neural analogue of our warp), FNO, NOMAD, and a convolutional-autoencoder manifold ROM. Extend the DeepONet learning-rate grid upward until the optimum is INTERIOR (l5_fill2 shows ~0.0275 at lr = 3e-3, on the old boundary). Restate the L5 verdict as 'linear-reconstruction operator learning is eliminated', with the Lanthaler et al. lower bound cited as the reason.
concrete_actions.rationale: As designed, L5 tested only architectures that theory already condemns, using a grid whose optimum sat on the boundary. Both are fatal to the claim as written. Fixing them costs compute, not ideas, and turns the weakest rung into a rung that engages current theory.

concrete_actions.action: Run robust sPOD (Krah et al., arXiv:2403.04313; public code) and a quadratic approximation manifold (Barnett & Farhat, arXiv:2204.02462) on the same 988 fields with the same nRMSE normalisation. Report both against the fixed frame and the two-wave frame.
concrete_actions.rationale: sPOD is the field-standard multi-transport method and its absence is the most predictable referee demand; it is also the additive counterpart to our compositional warp, so the comparison directly tests our central claim. The quadratic manifold is a decisive control: if it approaches 0.02 without any front tracking, the warp is unnecessary and we need to know that before submission, not after.

concrete_actions.action: Replace the ad-hoc span clamp with a monotonicity-by-construction parameterisation, and upgrade the regressor. Represent the warp in SRVF / Fisher-Rao coordinates (Srivastava et al., arXiv:1103.3817) or keep (t_lo, log-span) but bound it so every prediction is a valid monotone warp. Compare HistGradientBoosting against POD-plus-cross-validated-Gaussian-RBF (the CDI recipe, Cucchiara et al. arXiv:2310.04290 section 2.3) and greedy kernel VKOGA (Herkert et al., arXiv:2405.19170), which was designed for scarce-data breakthrough-curve prediction specifically.
concrete_actions.rationale: hi_pred = max(hi_pred, lo_pred + 1e-3) is a visible hack that a statistically literate referee will flag as unprincipled. The two suggested regressors are the published state of the art for this exact sub-problem - one from the registration-MOR literature, one from our own application domain - and both are cheap to run.

concrete_actions.action: Add one paragraph tying the measured d_n ~ n^-1.23 to Arbes, Greif & Urban (arXiv:2305.00066): their sharp result d_n ~ c_r n^{-r} for data in H^{r-eps} means our exponent is a measurement of front regularity (fronts smoothed by LDF kinetics and axial dispersion, near H^1.2), which is why we do not observe the classical n^{-1/2} of a true jump. Keep the existing n = 8-64 scoping caveat.
concrete_actions.rationale: Two sentences convert a curve fit into a theoretically grounded statement, and pre-empt the obvious question of why our exponent differs from the transport literature's canonical N^{-1/2}.

concrete_actions.action: Reconcile the learning curve with the L1 verdict before submission, or restrict L1 explicitly. State that in the two-wave frame the error improves 1.82x (0.0929 -> 0.0509) from 12 to 48 training materials without saturating, and either finish data/parametric_scale (currently ~1457 of 4080 runs, no manifest) to settle it, or narrow L1's claim to the operating-condition axis only.
concrete_actions.rationale: Publishing 'more data is eliminated' while an unsaturated material-axis learning curve sits in the same repository is a self-inflicted integrity problem. A project whose entire identity is falsification cannot leave a known counter-measurement unaddressed - and the honest, scoped version ('data helps on the material axis and not the condition axis') is a more interesting result than the blanket one.

concrete_actions.action: Write the related-work section around the Acta Numerica 2026 taxonomy (Hesthaven, Peherstorfer & Unger, arXiv:2602.01397), locating each of our experiments in it: fixed-frame POD+GBM as the linear baseline, single-front alignment as the freezing/calibration family (Ohlberger & Rave 2013; Cagniart-Maday-Stamm 2019), the two-wave warp as landmark registration (Taddei 2020; Sarna et al. 2024; Cucchiara et al. 2024; Labatut et al. 2026), and DeepONet as linear-reconstruction operator learning bounded below by Lanthaler et al. (2023). Add a prepared paragraph on why Wasserstein methods (Ehrlacher et al., M2AN 54, 2020) do not apply directly - our c-field is a saturating breakthrough profile, not a conserved density.
concrete_actions.rationale: A February-2026 Acta Numerica survey exists and defines the vocabulary the reviewers will use. Writing to it makes the paper legible to that community, and the pre-emptive Wasserstein paragraph closes the most likely 'why didn't you use optimal transport?' objection before it is asked.

concrete_actions.action: Test adaptive alignment levels and adaptive time partitioning as cheap alternatives: choose the (lo, hi) crossing pair per sample rather than fixing (0.05, 0.95), following the adaptivity of Barral, Taddei & Tifouti (JCP 499:112727, 2024); and test goal-oriented piecewise-linear time partitioning (Jin, Peng & Xiang, arXiv:2505.08214) as a warp-free competitor.
concrete_actions.rationale: Our level pair is hand-picked and one of the three we tried (0.20-0.80) was contaminated by its interpolation floor - a referee will ask how sensitive the result is to that choice. Partitioning is the simplest published alternative to warping for a widely varying feature separation and should be ruled in or out on evidence rather than by omission.

concrete_actions.action: Fetch and read the two references I could confirm only from search results before citing them: Zucatti & Zahr, 'Model reduction of convection-dominated viscous conservation laws using implicit feature tracking and landmark image registration' (arXiv:2503.17463, 2025), and Krah, Buechholz, Haeringer & Reiss, 'Front Transport Reduction for Complex Moving Fronts' (arXiv:2202.08208; J. Sci. Comput. 96, 2023).
concrete_actions.rationale: Both use the exact vocabulary of our contribution ('landmark registration'; 'front shape function composed with a distance-to-front coordinate') and are the most likely sources of an unanticipated novelty collision. I verified their identity but not their contents, and this project's own standard forbids citing what has not been read.

lens: MOF/COF atmospheric water harvesting — the physical and experimental literature: citable isotherm parameters, thermophysical constants, published water breakthrough curves, isosteric heats, LDF mass-transfer coefficients, and the physically realistic Damköhler window for water in MOF pellets.

papers.citation: Farhad Fathieh, Markus J. Kalmutzki, Eugene A. Kapustin, Peter J. Waller, Jingjing Yang, Omar M. Yaghi, "Practical water production from desert air", Science Advances 4, eaat3198
papers.what_it_shows: MOF-303 [Al(OH)(HPDC)]: free pore volume 0.54 cm3/g; maximum water capture capacity 0.48 g/g (= 26.7 mol/kg); Type IV isotherm with inflection point at P/P0 = 0.15 and plateau reached at P/P0 = 0.30; 150 adsorption-desorption cycles with no measurable degradation; isotherms measured at 15, 25 and 85 C. MOF-801 device used 1.2 kg MOF; MOF-303/G 0.450 kg produced up to 105 g water/cycle; packing porosity 0.7 assumed for MOF-801/G, ~0.65 for the desert bed. Isosteric heat vs loading is reported in figs. S8 (MOF-801) and S26 (MOF-303).
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the primary citable source that replaces retraction A4's placeholders for q_max and step_rh. q_max = 26.7 mol/kg and step_rh = 0.15 are directly quotable. Our sampled q_max range (8-30 mol/kg) contains it; our step_rh range (0.08-0.45) contains it. The 0.7 packing porosity is far above our sampled eps_t (0.30-0.48) and shows that the AWH literature's form factor is powder, not pellet.

papers.citation: Nikita Hanikel, Mathieu S. Prevot, Farhad Fathieh, Eugene A. Kapustin, Hao Lyu, Haoze Wang, Nicolas J. Diercks, T. Grant Glover, Omar M. Yaghi, "Rapid Cycling and Exceptional Yield in a Metal-Organic Framework Water Harvester", ACS Central Science 5, 1699-1706
papers.url_or_id: 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00745 (open access; full text read via PMC6813556)
papers.what_it_shows: MOF-303: water uptake 39 wt% (0.39 g/g) at 20% RH; inflection point ~12% RH; isosteric heat of adsorption ~52 kJ/mol. MOF-303, Al-fumarate and SAPO-34 all have heats of 50-54 kJ/mol. Dynamic uptake of a 3 mm thin MOF-303 layer in a TGA at 30 C: full saturation in ~10 min at 20% RH, 5 min at 30% RH, 3 min at 40% RH, fitted as monoexponential (R2 > 99%); complete regeneration in minutes at 85 C. All sorbent beds processed to 3 mm height at packing porosity ~0.7 (chosen to avoid the Knudsen regime for intercrystallite diffusion); flow laminar. Packed-bed harvester: complete uptake in 300 min at 39% RH, 400 min at 32% RH, not achieved in 450 min at 22% RH.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Gives us (i) a citable isosteric heat of 52 kJ/mol -> delta_H = -49.52 kJ/mol in our convention because our own gate B7 fixed q_st = -delta_H + RT (RT = 2.48 kJ/mol at 298 K); (ii) a directly citable LDF magnitude: monoexponential 95% filling in 180-600 s implies k_LDF ~ 5e-3 to 1.7e-2 1/s for MOF-303 POWDER, which brackets the upper half of our sampled [0.002, 0.05]; (iii) the crucial contrast that the same material in a real packed bed needs 300-400 min, i.e. an apparent k two orders of magnitude smaller. That contrast is the physical basis for extending our k_LDF range downward.

papers.citation: Thomas Lassitter, Nikita Hanikel, Dennis J. Coyle, Mohammad I. Hossain, Bryce Lipinski, Michael O'Brien, David B. Hall, Jon Hastings, Juan Borja, Travis O'Neil, S. Ephraim Neumann, David R. Moore, Omar M. Yaghi, T. Grant Glover, "Mass transfer in atmospheric water harvesting systems", Chemical Engineering Science 285, 119430
papers.what_it_shows: Concentration-swing frequency response (CSFR) measurement of water diffusion in MOF-303, MOF-333 and a 4/4-MTV MOF over 0.00005-0.05 Hz at 25 C (and 40 C for MOF-303). Both a micropore-diffusion model and an LDF model are fitted; the LDF approximates the micropore model everywhere EXCEPT where the isotherm is steepest (deviations at 12% RH for MOF-303, 15% for MTV, 20-22% for MOF-333). A minimum in transport diffusivity D_s/r^2 occurs exactly at the isotherm step; the corrected (Maxwell-Stefan) diffusivity is nearly constant, so the minimum is thermodynamic, not mobility. Crystal size (powder vs ~20 um crystals) does NOT change D_s/r^2. Section 3.2: MOF-303 pressed into binder-free pellets, 3.11 g in a 1.5-inch-diameter tube, ambient air pulled through; Fig. 10 is the experimental water breakthrough curve with a 2-D axisymmetric COMSOL model overlay. The paper states explicitly that the unusual breakthrough shape is caused by the Type IV/V isotherm's inflection (favorable-to-unfavorable transition, shock-like then dispersed), citing LeVan & Carta and Bozbiyik et al. Coated tube: 3D-printed Inconel 1/4-inch tube, 6.395 cm long, 0.21 mm MOF coating; composite density 183.2 kg/m3, porosity 0.584, skeletal density 440 kg/m3. Tabulated mass-transfer data are in the SI.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The single most useful paper for us. (1) Fig. 10 is a digitisable, published, experimental water breakthrough curve on MOF-303 pellets with a validated model overlay - this is the fastest route to closing open item 2. (2) It states in print that the two-stage breakthrough shape is an isotherm-inflection effect, which is an independent, citable confirmation of our KEY PHYSICS FINDING (the two-wave breakthrough) and is the direct literature grounding for our two-wave warp. (3) It is the citable authority that the LDF assumption degrades exactly at the isotherm step - i.e. our LDF closure is weakest precisely where our cooperative shock lives. That is an honest limitation we must state rather than have a referee find. (4) SI tabulates D_s/r^2 values we can quote for k_LDF.

papers.citation: Belgin Bozbiyik, Tom Van Assche, Jeroen Lannoeye, Dirk E. De Vos, Gino V. Baron, Joeri F. M. Denayer, "Stepped water isotherm and breakthrough curves on aluminium fumarate metal-organic framework: experimental and modelling study", Adsorption 23(1), 185-192
papers.what_it_shows: Abstract verbatim: water vapour on Al-fumarate studied gravimetrically and in fixed beds. A two-step, Type IV water isotherm. Breakthrough experiments at feed conditions in three different zones of the isotherm. At LOW water partial pressure a SINGLE breakthrough step is observed; at HIGHER partial pressure a STEPPED (multi-wave) profile appears. The curves are described qualitatively by a simple model accounting for isotherm shape.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the canonical experimental precedent for our two-wave breakthrough, in the exact configuration we simulate (fixed bed, water, stepped-isotherm MOF) and with the exact dependence we find (wave separation is a function of the operating point relative to the step). It is the citation that converts our two-wave warp from 'a trick we noticed in synthetic data' into 'the exploitation of a documented experimental phenomenon'. It also gives a second digitisable breakthrough dataset. CAVEAT: I could not open the full text (Springer paywall), so I have NOT verified the figure numbers, column dimensions, particle size, voidage, flow rate, temperature, or any LDF value. Those must be read off the PDF before quoting.

papers.citation: Hyunho Kim, Sameer R. Rao, Eugene A. Kapustin, Lin Zhao, Sungwoo Yang, Omar M. Yaghi, Evelyn N. Wang, "Adsorption-based atmospheric water harvesting device for arid climates", Nature Communications 9, 1191
papers.what_it_shows: MOF-801 water isotherms at 15, 25, 45, 65 and 85 C; equilibrium uptake ~0.25 kg/kg at 15-25 C and ~30% RH; complete desorption at ~77 C and 10% RH. Bed properties: packing porosity 0.67, packing (bulk) density 464 kg/m3, MOF layer thickness 2.57 mm, particle density rho_p = 1400 +/- 20 kg/m3, skeletal density 2699.1 kg/m3, pore volume 0.3425 cm3/g. MOF-801 crystal diameter ~0.6 um with estimated effective intercrystalline vapour diffusivities.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: The only fully citable set of packed-bed thermophysical constants for an AWH MOF: particle density 1400 kg/m3 (our sampled rho_p range is 700-1400, so 1400 sits exactly on our upper bound), bed porosity 0.67, bulk density 464 kg/m3. Directly replaces the uncited rho_p = 1200 default in solver_fd.py. It also shows our eps_t sampling (0.30-0.48) does not overlap the porosity actually used in AWH beds.

papers.citation: Adam J. Rieth, Sungwoo Yang, Evelyn N. Wang, Mircea Dinca, "Record Atmospheric Fresh Water Capture and Heat Transfer with a Material Operating at the Water Uptake Reversibility Limit", ACS Central Science 3, 668-672
papers.what_it_shows: Co2Cl2BTDD (compound 2) and Co2Br2BTDD (3): Type IV isotherms at 298 K with the uptake step at 0.28 P/P0 (28% RH). Total water uptake at 94% RH: 0.968 g/g (Co2Cl2BTDD) and 0.766 g/g (Co2Br2BTDD). BET surface areas 1912 and 1762 m2/g after water sorption. Heat of adsorption from variable-temperature isotherms + Clausius-Clapeyron: ~55 kJ/mol at zero coverage FALLING to 45.8 kJ/mol during pore filling (vs 40.7 kJ/mol heat of vaporisation). Deliverable capacity 84.7 wt% under simulated desert day/night cycling, declining 5.1 wt% over 6 cycles; >1 g/g initial capacity with 6.3 wt% decline over 30 AHP cycles.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Two things. (1) It gives a fully citable high-capacity endmember: 0.968 g/g = 53.9 mol/kg, which is ABOVE our sampled q_max ceiling of 30 mol/kg - our material space truncates the best real AWH sorbent. (2) It is the cleanest published demonstration that q_st for water in a cooperative MOF is NOT constant with loading (55 -> 45.8 kJ/mol). Our dual-term Do-Do isotherm gives both terms the same delta_H and therefore enforces q_st = -delta_H exactly at every loading by construction (isotherm.py docstring says so). A referee who knows this literature will flag it. It is a stateable limitation and a natural extension (separate delta_H for the Henry and cluster terms).

papers.citation: Adam J. Rieth, Ashley M. Wright, Grigorii Skorupskii, Jenna L. Mancuso, Christopher H. Hendon, Mircea Dinca, "Record-Setting Sorbents for Reversible Water Uptake by Systematic Anion Exchanges in Metal-Organic Frameworks", Journal of the American Chemical Society 141, 13858-13866
papers.what_it_shows: Ni2Cl2BTDD: 1.07 g/g water uptake at 25 C, isotherm step at 32% RH, BET 1837 m2/g, pore diameter 2.3 nm, 98% capacity retained over 400 cycles, heat of adsorption ~-57 kJ/mol at zero coverage. Ni2Br2BTDD: 0.76 g/g (0.64 g/g below 25% RH), 0.581 cm3/cm3 volumetric, step at 24% RH, BET 1467 m2/g, pore 2.2 nm. Ni2F0.83Cl0.17BTDD: BET 1770 m2/g, step ~32% RH, poor cycling. Ni2(OH)2BTDD: BET 1792 m2/g, poor cycling.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: Gives an anion-tuned family of real materials whose step positions span 24-32% RH at nearly constant chemistry - i.e. published evidence that step_rh is an independently tunable material axis, which is exactly the axis our MATERIAL_SPACE varies. It also confirms the 53-59 mol/kg capacity ceiling that our q_max range truncates.

papers.citation: Ha L. Nguyen, Nikita Hanikel, Steven J. Lyle, Chenhui Zhu, Davide M. Proserpio, Omar M. Yaghi, "A Porous Covalent Organic Framework with Voided Square Grid Topology for Atmospheric Water Harvesting", Journal of the American Chemical Society 142, 2218-2221
papers.what_it_shows: COF-432, an imine-linked 2D COF (ETTA + TFB, mtf topology). BET surface area 895 m2/g (theoretical 900). N2 pore volume 0.43 cm3/g (PLATON 0.45). Single pore diameter 8.0 A from PSD; 1D cylindrical channel ~7.5 A. S-shaped, hysteresis-free water isotherm with steep pore-filling step at 34% RH at 25 C; maximal uptake at P/Psat = 0.95 is 30 wt% (0.30 g/g); working capacity between 20 and 40% RH is 0.23 g/g. Isotherms at 10, 25 and 40 C give an isosteric heat of ~48 kJ/mol (vs 44 kJ/mol water vaporisation enthalpy). 300 isobaric cycles at 1.7 kPa with a 30-35 C swing, working capacity unchanged.
papers.why_it_matters_to_us: This is the COF case that closes open item 3. Every number needed to instantiate our Do-Do form is present and citable: q_max = 0.30 g/g = 16.7 mol/kg, step at P/P0 = 0.34 (inside our step_rh range 0.08-0.45), q_st = 48 kJ/mol -> delta_H = -45.52 kJ/mol in our convention. A single COF condition set makes the title honest without any new solver work.

papers.citation: Bo Zhang, Zerui Zhu, Xuerui Wang, Xinlei Liu, Freek Kapteijn, "Water Adsorption in MOFs: Structures and Applications", Advanced Functional Materials 34, 2304788

That is exactly the functional form our k_LDF sampling should be derived from rather than drawn uniformly: k_LDF = 15 Dso exp(-Ea/RT)/Rp^2 makes k_LDF a FUNCTION of temperature and particle size instead of an independent uniform draw, which is both more defensible and removes a spurious degree of freedom from our material space. It also gives the temperature-shifted step (0.25 -> 0.33 over 30 -> 60 C), a direct test of whether our van't Hoff step shift is quantitatively right. Our model holds k_LDF constant per material. This is the strongest single technical criticism a referee from this community can make of our forward model, and it is also an obvious high-value extension: make k_LDF = k_corrected / (dq*/dc) and the kinetic and equilibrium axes stop being independent - which is directly relevant to L6's finding that k_LDF is unrecoverable from observable descriptors. state_of_the_art:
As of 2026 the physical/experimental AWH literature is in a very different place from the surrogate-modelling literature, and that mismatch is the project's main exposure.

EQUILIBRIUM. Water isotherms for the AWH-class frameworks are settled, tabulated and reproducible. The community reports each material as a triple (maximum uptake in g/g, step position in p/p0 at 298 K, isosteric heat as a range over loading). Representative published values: MOF-303 0.45-0.48 g/g, step 0.12-0.15, q_st ~52 kJ/mol falling toward 40 at high loading; MOF-801 0.36 g/g, step 0.09, 62->47 kJ/mol; MOF-841 0.51 g/g, step 0.22, 58->42; CAU-10-H 0.37 g/g, step 0.16, ~50-56; Al-fumarate 0.45 g/g, step 0.25-0.33 (temperature-dependent), 52.2 kJ/mol; Co2Cl2BTDD 0.97 g/g, step 0.28-0.29, 55->45.8; Ni2Cl2BTDD 1.07 g/g, step 0.32, ~57 at zero coverage; COF-432 0.30 g/g, step 0.34, ~48 kJ/mol. Two features are universal and both are absent from our forward model: q_st is a DECREASING function of loading (typically -10 to -15 kJ/mol from zero coverage to pore filling), and the step position shifts with temperature (Al-fumarate 0.25 -> 0.33 over 30 -> 60 C). Fitting practice is split between Dubinin-Astakhov / characteristic-curve (the thermal-engineering side) and dual-site Langmuir-association or Hill-type cooperative forms (the chemistry side); a 2025 Adsorption paper proposes an explicit dual-site Langmuir-association model for Al-fumarate/water, which is the closest published analogue of our dual-term Do-Do form.

KINETICS. This is where the state of the art has moved most and where our model is furthest behind. The best current measurement technique is concentration-swing frequency response (CSFR), which fits BOTH a micropore-diffusion model and an LDF model to the same data. The headline 2024 result (Lassitter et al., Chem. Eng. Sci. 285, 119430) is that for water in MOF-303/MOF-333/MTV-MOF the LDF approximation is good everywhere EXCEPT at the isotherm step, where it produces a visibly wrong response shape; and that the observed transport rate D_s/r^2 has a MINIMUM at the step, which is a thermodynamic effect (rate = corrected diffusivity / isotherm slope) rather than a mobility effect. The corrected (Maxwell-Stefan) diffusivity is nearly constant. Crystal size did not change D_s/r^2, implying the controlling length scale is the aggregate, not the crystal. When the same MOF is put in a polymer binder, MACROpore diffusion takes over from micropore diffusion entirely. So the modern view is: for a real pellet or coating, k_LDF is macropore-controlled, concentration-dependent through the isotherm slope, and dips by roughly an order of magnitude exactly where a cooperative step sits.

DYNAMICS / COLUMNS. There is a small but real experimental literature on water breakthrough in MOF beds, and it says the same thing our simulations found. Bozbiyik et al. (2017) measured Al-fumarate fixed-bed breakthrough at three feed humidities spanning the isotherm's zones and observed a SINGLE step at low feed partial pressure and a STEPPED (multi-wave) profile at higher feed pressure. Lassitter et al. (2024) measured a MOF-303 pellet breakthrough (Fig. 10) and state explicitly that its unusual shape comes from the isotherm inflection - the favorable-to-unfavorable transition producing a shock-like segment followed by a dispersed segment - citing LeVan & Carta and Bozbiyik. Li et al. (2025, RSC Adv, open access) report MOF-303 breakthrough in a 0.6 cm ID, ~10 cm bed at 298 K and 300 sccm. So the two-wave breakthrough is a documented, experimentally reproduced, mechanistically explained phenomenon, not a novelty - but no one has exploited it as a coordinate transform for reduced-order modelling, which is where our contribution lives.

BED CONSTANTS. Published AWH beds are POWDER or thin-layer beds, not pellet beds: packing porosity 0.65-0.70 (Fathieh 2018 ~0.65-0.7, Hanikel 2019 ~0.7, Kim 2018 0.67), bulk packing density ~464 kg/m3, particle density 1400 +/- 20 kg/m3, layer thickness 2.57-3 mm. Pellet-bed constants (voidage 0.35-0.42, d_p 1-3 mm) are the classical packed-bed values from Ruthven and are what a chemical-engineering referee will expect if the column is 10 cm long. Solid heat capacity is a genuine gap: I could not find a directly citable measured C_p for MOF-303, MOF-801, CAU-10-H or any COF in this search. The AWH literature typically argues q_sensible << q_latent and never reports C_p, so our C_ps = 1000 J/kg/K has no source. That is a real, currently unresolved citation hole.

MACHINE LEARNING IN THIS LENS. Work is almost entirely on EQUILIBRIUM screening (structure -> isotherm / working capacity), e.g. "Machine Learning Highlights Chemistry as the Key Factor in MOFs for Atmospheric Water Harvesting" (2025). Surrogate models for the DYNAMIC column problem in AWH are essentially unoccupied. That is genuinely good news for the project's positioning - but it also means no referee will accept a purely synthetic study without at least one anchor to a measured curve.
implications: The two-wave breakthrough is NOT our discovery; it is a published, experimentally observed, mechanistically explained phenomenon (Bozbiyik 2017 for Al-fumarate; Lassitter 2024 Fig. 10 for MOF-303 pellets, explicitly attributed to the Type IV/V inflection and the favorable->unfavorable transition, citing LeVan & Carta). This is much better for us than it sounds. It converts our KEY PHYSICS FINDING from an unverified claim about a synthetic dataset into a reproduction of a documented experimental effect, and it converts the two-wave warp from a numerical trick into 'a coordinate change derived from the known wave structure of inflected-isotherm systems'. But the manuscript must cite it up front. Claiming the two-wave structure as novel physics would be a serious and easily-caught error.

Our sampled parameter space is defensible on four axes and broken on three. Defensible: step_rh [0.08, 0.45] covers all real steps (0.09-0.34); delta_H [-60, -38] kJ/mol covers real q_st 45-58 kJ/mol given our own q_st = -delta_H + RT convention (gate B7); rho_p [700, 1400] contains the only measured AWH value (1400 kg/m3, Kim 2018); the Type V / cooperative form is exactly what the neutron-diffraction and cluster-nucleation literature says is happening. Broken: (i) q_max ceiling 30 mol/kg truncates the best real sorbents - Co2Cl2BTDD is 53.9 mol/kg and Ni2Cl2BTDD is 59.4 mol/kg; (ii) eps_t [0.30, 0.48] is a pellet-bed range while every published AWH bed is 0.65-0.70; (iii) isotherm_n [1, 6] under-covers the sharpest steps - from published 10-90% step widths the implied Hill exponent is ~3.6-5.6 for MOF-303 (inside range) but ~7 for CAU-10-H, ~10 for Al-fumarate, ~12 for COF-432 and ~15 for Co2Cl2BTDD (all outside). (These n values are MY arithmetic from published step positions, n = ln(81)/ln(rh90/rh10), not published fits, and should be checked against digitised isotherms before being quoted.)

The k_LDF range is internally inconsistent with our own particle diameter, and the inconsistency is large. solver_fd.py fixes d_p = 0.002 m, but a Glueckauf macropore-controlled estimate at that size gives k_LDF ~= 4.9e-4 1/s, while MATERIAL_SPACE samples k_LDF in [0.002, 0.05] - between 4x and 100x too fast for a 2 mm pellet. The sampled range actually corresponds to d_p ~= 0.2-1.0 mm (fine beads or powder), which is consistent with the MOF-303 powder TGA data (Hanikel 2019: 95% filling in 180-600 s => k ~5e-3 to 1.7e-2 1/s) but not with the stated geometry. A referee who computes 15*eps_p*D_p/(R_p^2 * rho_p * dq/dc) will find this in ten minutes.

Da ~ 1-50 is not merely reachable, it is what real pelletised MOF columns actually sit at. Using our own Da = k_LDF * t_final definition, with the published MOF-303 equilibrium (0.45 g/g, 25 mol/kg), rho_p = 1200, eps = 0.40, L = 0.10 m and 30% RH feed: a 2 mm pellet (k = 4.9e-4) gives Da = 51 at v = 0.10 m/s and Da = 17 at v = 0.30 m/s; a 3 mm pellet gives Da = 23 and Da = 8. So the 'informative regime' the protocol identified is exactly the pelletised-MOF regime, and our current Da 155-3885 corresponds to POWDER beds (0.2-0.5 mm) - which are what the AWH device literature uses, but not what a 10 cm packed column would use. Both regimes are physical; they are different form factors, and the paper should say which one it is modelling.

There is a hard floor below which extending Da becomes unphysical, and it is around Da ~ 3-5 (our definition), not 1. The mass-transfer-zone width in our own mtz_width() is u_front/k_LDF; the MTZ equals the whole bed when N = k*L/u_front ~= 1, i.e. Da ~= 2.5. Below that the bed cannot form a front at all and the exit curve degenerates toward a single-CSTR exponential - a regime no one designs a column in and where the two-wave structure the paper is about ceases to exist. Recommendation: extend down to Da ~ 5, not to Da ~ 1, and state the floor and its reason.

Our LDF closure is weakest exactly where our cooperative shock lives, and this is documented in print. Lassitter et al. show the LDF fit deviates from the micropore model specifically at the steep part of the isotherm (12% RH for MOF-303, 20-22% for MOF-333), and that D_s/r^2 has a MINIMUM there because rate = corrected diffusivity / isotherm slope. Our model uses a single constant k_LDF per material, independent of loading. This is a real modelling limitation, it must be stated, and it interacts directly with L6: the reason k_LDF is unrecoverable from observable descriptors in our data (R^2 = -0.61) may be partly that a constant-k model is not the right kinetic object for this physics in the first place.

Our constant isosteric heat is a construction artefact that this literature contradicts uniformly. isotherm.py deliberately gives both the Henry and cluster terms the same delta_H so that 'the isosteric heat is exactly -dH at every loading and Clausius-Clapeyron is satisfied by construction'. Every measured AWH material shows q_st falling with loading: Co2Cl2BTDD 55 -> 45.8 kJ/mol (measured, Clausius-Clapeyron, Rieth 2017); MOF-801 62 -> 47; MOF-841 58 -> 42; MOF-303 50 -> 40. Since the energy balance couples through (-delta_H) dq/dt and the thermal wave is what broadens our front (documented in mtz_width's own caveat, a 26x effect), a 20-25% loading-dependent variation in q_st is not a second-order detail for the two-wave separation we are trying to predict.

We now have three digitisable published water breakthrough datasets, which is enough to close open item 2. Ranked by usefulness: (1) Li et al. 2025 RSC Adv Fig. 11 - open access, MOF-303, bed height ~10 cm = our L exactly, 0.6 cm ID, 300 sccm => superficial v = 0.177 m/s which is inside our sampled v range, 298 K which is inside our T range. Zero geometry rescaling needed. (2) Lassitter et al. 2024 Fig. 10 - MOF-303 binder-free pellets, 3.11 g, 1.5 inch tube, ambient air, with a validated COMSOL overlay to check our solver against a second independent model. (3) Bozbiyik et al. 2017 - Al-fumarate at three feed humidities, the only dataset that directly shows the single-step -> stepped transition and therefore the only one that can validate the TWO-WAVE structure rather than just the mean breakthrough time.

The COF gap is closable today with COF-432, and the COF DYNAMICS gap is a genuine open frontier. Nguyen et al. 2020 gives every number needed: q_max 0.30 g/g = 16.7 mol/kg, step at 34% RH at 25 C, q_st ~48 kJ/mol (=> delta_H = -45.52 kJ/mol in our convention), pore volume 0.43 cm3/g, 300 cycles stable. Separately, I found NO published experimental packed-bed water breakthrough curve for any COF in this search. That is worth stating as a limitation and as motivation: a simulated COF column is the only kind that currently exists.

Solid heat capacity is our one remaining uncited constant with no source found. C_ps = 1000 J/kg/K in solver_fd.py has no literature anchor for any of these frameworks; the AWH papers argue q_sensible << q_latent and simply do not report it. Since beta = (1-eps) rho_p (-dH) q_ref / (C_term T_ref) is one of our seven dimensionless groups and the thermal wave dominates the front width, this is not a harmless default. It needs either a measured value from the MOF calorimetry literature (search for Mu & Walton-type C_p measurements on MOF-5/HKUST-1/UiO-66 as a bracket) or an explicit sensitivity study reported in the paper.
risks_to_our_claims: NOVELTY OF THE TWO-WAVE PHYSICS. A referee from this community will immediately recognise the two-wave breakthrough from Bozbiyik et al. (2017) and Lassitter et al. (2024, which states the mechanism in plain text and cites LeVan & Carta for it). If the manuscript presents 'the Type V isotherm produces a two-wave breakthrough' as a finding rather than as a reproduction, the paper's credibility takes a hit that is disproportionate to the actual error, because the project's whole selling point is epistemic discipline. Fix by citing it as prior art and claiming only the WARP as new.

PARAMETER PROVENANCE. Retraction A4 is currently a submission blocker in the most literal sense: with q_max = 20 mol/kg, C_ps = 1000, rho_p = 1200 and a hand-chosen b0, no reviewer will accept any material-specific language. Worse, a reviewer who checks will find that the sampled k_LDF range is 4-100x inconsistent with the stated 2 mm particle diameter in the same config file. That is exactly the kind of internal inconsistency this project's own RETRACTIONS.md discipline exists to catch, and having a referee find it first would be damaging.

REGIME RELEVANCE. The strongest available attack is: 'you have simulated 988 near-equilibrium columns (Da 155-3885, median driving force 1.38% of q_max, 44% of conditions never exceeding 1%) and then concluded that kinetic identification is impossible. That conclusion is a property of your sampling, not of the problem.' The protocol already concedes this at section on identifiability. Until the low-Da dataset exists, L6's NOT SUPPORTED verdict and the k_LDF unrecoverability result are both defensible only as regime-conditional statements, and must be worded that way everywhere including the abstract.

CONSTANT k_LDF AND CONSTANT q_st. Two independent, well-documented physical effects are absent from the forward model, and both act precisely at the cooperative step, which is precisely where the second wave is: (a) the transport rate has a minimum at the step because rate = corrected diffusivity / isotherm slope (Lassitter 2024 for MOF-303/333/MTV; Hossain & Glover 2019 for UiO-66); (b) q_st falls 10-15 kJ/mol from zero coverage to pore filling in every measured AWH material. A referee can argue that the second wave's position and width - the thing the whole warp is fitted to - is quantitatively wrong for both reasons, and that the 40x variation in t(0.9)-t(0.1) across the dataset is therefore partly an artefact of an over-simple closure.

BED FORM FACTOR. The manuscript currently mixes regimes: eps_t 0.30-0.48 (pellet bed), d_p 2 mm (pellet), L 0.10 m (lab column), but k_LDF 0.002-0.05 (powder) and a materials list drawn from AWH device papers whose beds are all 0.65-0.70 porosity powder layers 2.6-3 mm thick. A reviewer can reasonably ask which physical system is being modelled and note that no real device matches the combination.

LDF VALIDITY AT THE STEP. Lassitter et al. is explicit that the LDF model produces a distinctly wrong response shape at the isotherm step and that the micropore model is required there. Since the entire paper is about resolving structure at and around the step, 'your kinetic closure is known to fail exactly in your region of interest' is a legitimate and quotable objection with a 2024 citation behind it.

NO EXPERIMENTAL ANCHOR AT ALL. For a top-tier venue, a purely synthetic surrogate study with a verified solver but zero contact with measurement is a hard sell in a field (adsorption engineering / AWH) whose journals expect experimental grounding. Three digitisable curves now exist and one of them (Li 2025) matches our geometry almost exactly; not using them will read as unwillingness rather than unavailability.

TITLE-vs-CONTENT ON COFs. Claiming a COF in the title with no COF case is straightforwardly indefensible, and the fix is cheap (COF-432 is fully parameterised in Nguyen et al. 2020). Leaving it is a gratuitous risk.

q_max TRUNCATION. If the paper says the material space 'spans realistic AWH frameworks' while capping q_max at 30 mol/kg, a referee can point at Co2Cl2BTDD (53.9 mol/kg) and Ni2Cl2BTDD (59.4 mol/kg) - the two record-setting materials in the field - and note they fall outside. Either widen the range or state the truncation and its reason explicitly.

THE SPEED CLAIM. Retraction A6 is right that 'hours per simulation' is indefensible for a 1-D column. Note that Lassitter et al. solved this exact class of problem with a 2-D axisymmetric COMSOL model and did not report it as expensive. Any per-simulation speedup framing invites a reviewer to point at that.

concrete_actions.action: Replace every placeholder in solver_fd.py / MATERIAL_SPACE with cited values and add a `references` field per material. Concretely: q_max 25.0 mol/kg (= 0.45 g/g, Zhang 2023 Table 1) or 26.7 mol/kg (= 0.48 g/g, Fathieh 2018) for MOF-303; step_rh 0.13 (Zhang) / 0.12 (Hanikel 2019) / 0.15 (Fathieh); delta_H = -49.52 kJ/mol (from q_st = 52 kJ/mol, Hanikel 2019, using our own q_st = -delta_H + RT convention from gate B7); rho_p = 1400 kg/m3 (Kim 2018 Nat Commun, measured for MOF-801); bed porosity 0.67 (Kim 2018) or 0.70 (Hanikel 2019) if modelling a powder bed. Add COF-432 (q_max 16.7 mol/kg, step 0.34, delta_H = -45.52 kJ/mol from q_st 48, Nguyen 2020), CAU-10-H (20.6 mol/kg, step 0.16, q_st 50-56), MOF-801 (20.0, 0.09, 62-47), MOF-841 (28.3, 0.22, 58-42), Al-fumarate (25.0, 0.25-0.33 T-dependent, 52.2), Co2Cl2BTDD (53.9, 0.28, 55->45.8).
concrete_actions.rationale: Retraction A4 is the stated submission blocker and every number above is now traced to a verified primary source. Doing this also lets the manuscript say 'the sampled space is calibrated against N published frameworks' with a table, which is far stronger than 'literature-range'.

concrete_actions.action: Fix the k_LDF / d_p inconsistency by deriving k_LDF from particle size instead of sampling it independently. Use the Glueckauf macropore-controlled form k_LDF = 15 eps_p D_p / (R_p^2 rho_p (dq*/dc)) with D_p = D_m/tau, D_m = 2.6e-5 m2/s, eps_p ~ 0.35, tau ~ 3, plus the external film resistance 1/k_ext = R_p rho_p K/(3 k_f) with k_f from Sh = 2 + 1.1 Sc^0.33 Re^0.6. My computed values at 30% RH, 298 K, MOF-303 equilibrium, rho_p = 1200: d_p = 0.5 mm -> k = 7.1e-3 1/s; 1 mm -> 1.9e-3; 2 mm -> 4.9e-4 (macropore is 84% of the resistance); 3 mm -> 2.2e-4. Then sample d_p over 0.5-3 mm rather than sampling k_LDF uniformly, or at minimum change d_p to match the k range that is already sampled.
concrete_actions.rationale: As written, MATERIAL_SPACE k_LDF [0.002, 0.05] with d_p fixed at 2 mm is physically self-contradictory by 4-100x and a referee can check it with one calculation. Deriving k from d_p also removes a spurious free parameter, ties the kinetic axis to a measurable geometric quantity, and makes the low-Da extension a statement about pellet size (which is what an engineer controls) rather than about an abstract rate constant.

concrete_actions.action: Generate the low-Damkohler dataset by extending d_p / lowering k_LDF down to Da ~= 5, NOT Da ~= 1, and state the floor. Target k_LDF down to ~1e-4 1/s (a 3-5 mm pellet). Justify the extension with the calculation above: a 2 mm MOF-303 pellet at v = 0.1 m/s gives Da = 51 and at v = 0.3 m/s gives Da = 17; a 3 mm pellet gives Da = 23 and Da = 8. Justify the floor with our own mtz_width(): the MTZ equals the whole bed when N = k L / u_front ~= 1, i.e. Da ~= 2.5, below which no front exists and the two-wave structure the paper studies ceases to be defined.
concrete_actions.rationale: This answers the user's direct question with a defence rather than an assertion: Da ~ 1-50 is not merely reachable, it is precisely the pelletised-column regime, while the current Da 155-3885 is the powder/thin-layer regime of AWH devices. Having the physical justification in hand converts a 'we should sample more' change into a 'we sampled the wrong form factor and here is the correction' change, which is a much better story - and it is the pre-declared re-test of H1.

concrete_actions.action: Digitise Li et al. 2025 RSC Adv Figure 11 (MOF-303 breakthrough) as the primary experimental anchor and Lassitter et al. 2024 Figure 10 as the secondary. The Li geometry needs no rescaling: bed height ~10 cm = our L = 0.10 m; 0.6 cm ID with 300 sccm gives superficial v = 0.177 m/s, inside our sampled [0.03, 0.30]; 298 K, inside our [288.15, 313.15]. Report a solver-vs-experiment error separately from the surrogate-vs-solver error, exactly as CONTINUE_HERE item 2 specifies.
concrete_actions.rationale: Closes the 'no experimental validation at all' blocker with the least possible work, because the published geometry already matches our configuration. Lassitter's Fig. 10 additionally carries a validated COMSOL overlay, so it doubles as an independent code-to-code check of our finite-difference solver against a commercial FEM solution of the same problem.

concrete_actions.action: Obtain the Bozbiyik et al. (2017) PDF and digitise all three breakthrough curves (low, intermediate and high water partial pressure). This is the only published dataset that shows the single-step -> stepped transition as the feed moves through the isotherm zones.
concrete_actions.rationale: It is the only experimental validation available for the TWO-WAVE STRUCTURE specifically, as opposed to the mean breakthrough time. Since the two-wave warp is the paper's one positive result, validating the wave structure rather than just the curve is what makes the contribution credible. It is also the citation that establishes the phenomenon as prior art, which we must do anyway.

concrete_actions.action: Rewrite the two-wave physics section to cite Bozbiyik (2017), Lassitter (2024) and LeVan & Carta as prior art for the phenomenon, and narrow the novelty claim to the warp coordinate itself. State plainly: the two-wave structure of inflected-isotherm breakthrough is documented experimentally and understood theoretically; what is new is using the two front trajectories as a nonlinear coordinate change that collapses the Kolmogorov n-width from 31 to 13-17 modes, and the measurement that this beats the best operator arm anywhere in the ladder (oracle warp 0.0203/0.0233 vs DeepONet 0.0281).
concrete_actions.rationale: Same class of correction as retraction A12 (DeepOKAN novelty), and the project's own standing rule 4 requires comparing against the strongest existing position. Doing it proactively is worth far more than having a referee do it, and the narrowed claim is genuinely strong and genuinely unoccupied.

concrete_actions.action: Add COF-432 as a named case using Nguyen et al. 2020: q_max = 0.30 g/g = 16.7 mol/kg, cooperative step at P/P0 = 0.34 at 298 K, q_st ~48 kJ/mol => delta_H = -45.52 kJ/mol, pore volume 0.43 cm3/g, BET 895 m2/g, 300 cycles with unchanged working capacity, working capacity 0.23 g/g between 20 and 40% RH. State explicitly that no experimental packed-bed water breakthrough curve exists for any COF, so the COF column is necessarily simulation-only, and use that as motivation rather than hiding it.
concrete_actions.rationale: Closes open item 3 (title claims a COF, none exists) with a single fully-parameterised, verified material and no new solver work. The honest statement about the missing COF dynamics literature is itself a contribution and pre-empts the obvious question of why there is no COF validation.

concrete_actions.action: Add a stated-limitations subsection covering the three closure simplifications this literature contradicts, each with its citation: (i) constant k_LDF per material, whereas the measured transport rate has a minimum at the isotherm step because rate = corrected diffusivity / isotherm slope (Lassitter 2024 for MOF-303/333/MTV; Hossain & Glover 2019 for UiO-66); (ii) LDF itself, which is documented to deviate from the micropore model specifically at the steep part of the isotherm (Lassitter 2024, Figs. 1-2, deviations at 12% RH for MOF-303 and 20-22% for MOF-333); (iii) constant isosteric heat, whereas every measured AWH material shows q_st falling with loading (Co2Cl2BTDD 55 -> 45.8 measured by Clausius-Clapeyron, MOF-801 62 -> 47, MOF-841 58 -> 42, MOF-303 50 -> 40).
concrete_actions.rationale: All three are checkable in ten minutes by anyone in this field, and all three sit exactly at the cooperative step where the paper's second wave lives. Declaring them, with citations, is consistent with the project's entire methodological stance and defuses the single most quotable technical objection.

concrete_actions.action: Run a sensitivity study on loading-dependent isosteric heat, or implement it. Minimal version: give the Henry and cluster terms different delta_H (e.g. -55 and -45 kJ/mol) so q_st interpolates from ~57 at zero coverage to ~47 at pore filling, matching Co2Cl2BTDD's measured 55 -> 45.8, and report how much the two-wave separation t(0.9)-t(0.1) moves. Note that the Clausius-Clapeyron gate (B7) must be generalised: it currently checks q_st = -delta_H + RT at a single value.
concrete_actions.rationale: The energy balance couples through (-delta_H) dq/dt, and mtz_width()'s own measured caveat says the thermal wave broadens the front by a factor of ~26 relative to the isothermal estimate. A 20-25% loading-dependent variation in the heat therefore acts directly on the quantity the warp is fitted to. If the sensitivity is small, that is a strong result to report; if it is large, we need to know before a referee does.

concrete_actions.action: Widen q_max to at least 55 mol/kg and isotherm_n to at least 12, or state and justify the truncation. Real endmembers: Co2Cl2BTDD 0.968 g/g = 53.9 mol/kg (Rieth 2017) and Ni2Cl2BTDD 1.07 g/g = 59.4 mol/kg (Rieth 2019). For cooperativity, n = ln(81)/ln(rh90/rh10) applied to published step widths gives ~3.6-5.6 for MOF-303, ~7 for CAU-10-H, ~10 for Al-fumarate, ~12 for COF-432 and ~15 for Co2Cl2BTDD - so [1, 6] covers only the mildest real steps. Verify these n values against digitised isotherms before quoting them; they are my arithmetic, not published fits.
concrete_actions.rationale: The two record-setting AWH materials in the field fall outside our q_max range, and the sharpest real steps fall outside our n range. Since the sharper the step the stronger the two-wave separation, truncating n at 6 may be systematically excluding the regime where our own method works best.

concrete_actions.action: Resolve or bound the solid heat capacity C_ps = 1000 J/kg/K. I could not find a citable measured C_p for MOF-303, MOF-801, CAU-10-H or any COF in this search - the AWH literature argues q_sensible << q_latent and omits it. Either find a measured value in the MOF calorimetry literature (search Mu & Walton-type C_p measurements on MOF-5 / HKUST-1 / UiO-66 as a bracket) or run and report an explicit sensitivity sweep over C_ps in the range 700-1100 J/kg/K showing the effect on beta and on the two-wave separation.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is the last uncited constant with no source found, and it enters one of the seven dimensionless groups (beta) that governs the thermal wave - which is the dominant front-broadening mechanism per mtz_width()'s own measured caveat. Leaving it as a bare default after fixing everything else would be conspicuous.

concrete_actions.action: Consider replacing the uniform k_LDF draw with an Arrhenius surface-diffusion parameterisation, k_LDF = 15 Dso exp(-Ea/RT)/Rp^2, following Teo et al. (2017), who report exactly this form (Dso, Ea, Rp) for water on aluminium fumarate. Obtain that PDF for the numeric constants. This also makes k_LDF temperature-dependent, which it currently is not.
concrete_actions.rationale: Makes the kinetic axis a function of temperature and particle radius rather than an independent uniform draw, which is both more physical and directly relevant to L6: part of why k_LDF is unrecoverable from observable descriptors (R^2 = -0.61) may be that in reality it is not an independent quantity at all. It also lets the manuscript cite a published parameterisation instead of defending a range.

concrete_actions.action: Decide and state the bed form factor explicitly, in one sentence in the methods. Either (a) a pellet-packed lab column: eps_t 0.35-0.42, d_p 1-3 mm, k_LDF 2e-4 to 2e-3 1/s, Da ~ 8-60 - the regime the digitisable breakthrough curves sit in and the classical packed-bed regime a chemical-engineering referee expects for a 10 cm column; or (b) an AWH device powder layer: eps_t 0.65-0.70, effective d_p 0.2-0.5 mm, k_LDF 5e-3 to 2e-2 1/s, Da ~ 600-4000 - the regime the AWH device papers report and the regime our current dataset is actually in. Do not mix them.
concrete_actions.rationale: The current configuration mixes the two (pellet d_p and eps_t with powder k_LDF), and no real system matches the combination. Choosing (a) aligns with the validation data and with the pre-declared low-Da re-test; choosing (b) aligns with the AWH device literature but makes L6's near-equilibrium verdict the headline. Either is defensible; the mixture is not.

concrete_actions.action: Add the modern AWH machine-learning context to the introduction and position against it: ML work in this field is almost entirely equilibrium screening (structure -> isotherm / working capacity), with 2025 examples such as 'Machine Learning Highlights Chemistry as the Key Factor in MOFs for Atmospheric Water Harvesting'. Surrogate modelling of the DYNAMIC AWH column is essentially unoccupied.
concrete_actions.rationale: This is a genuine and defensible positioning claim that raises the paper's apparent contribution without overstating anything, and it is currently missing. It also explains to a referee why a negative-result-heavy paper is worth publishing here: the field has not yet established what does and does not work on the dynamic problem, so the falsification ladder is filling a real void rather than re-deriving known results.

area: Manuscript: contamination audit of 01_INTRODUCTION.md / 02_METHODOLOGY_JUSTIFICATION.md / 00_MASTER_PLAN_DYNAMICS.md against the evidence in RESULTS.md, RETRACTIONS.md, 03_LADDER_PROTOCOL.md and the result JSONs; writing-quality assessment; and the specification of the paper the evidence actually supports.

findings.title: 01 and 02 are live, unmarked documents containing ~20 retracted claims, and no honesty gate covers prose
findings.evidence: Neither file carries any header, banner, or WITHDRAWN marker. They are named as manuscript Sections 1 and 2 ('# 1. Introduction', '# 2. Methodology & Architecture Justification') and sit in the repo root beside RESULTS.md. Meanwhile `grep -n "01_INTRO|02_METHOD|00_MASTER|\.md" validate.py` returns ZERO hits: all 22 gates read code and data, none reads a markdown file. The project asserts (03_LADDER_PROTOCOL.md:1506) '`validate.py` gates every claim. No number enters the manuscript from a failing category' — but the two files literally called the manuscript are outside the gate perimeter.
findings.why_it_matters: The project's entire credibility asset is that retracted claims are dead, not merely annotated elsewhere. A retraction ledger co-existing with a live, unmarked document that still says 'PIKAN extrapolates perfectly' and 'the first unified architecture' is worse than having no ledger: a referee who finds both concludes the ledger is decorative. This is also the single most likely mechanism by which a retracted sentence reaches a submission — copy-paste from the file named 'Introduction'.
findings.fix: Immediately rename to `_WITHDRAWN_01_INTRODUCTION.md` / `_WITHDRAWN_02_METHODOLOGY.md` (the repo already uses this convention: `results/l5_singlelr_WITHDRAWN.json`, `data/_RETRACTED`), prepend a banner naming the retractions each file carries, and add a validate.py gate `gate_no_withdrawn_prose` that fails if any un-prefixed .md in the repo root contains the strings 'Foundation Digital Twin', 'PI-DeepOKAN', 'pioneers', 'the first unified', 'fail catastrophically', or 'extrapolates perfectly'. Verify the gate fires by planting a violating file (CONTINUE_HERE.md trap 5).

findings.title: L1's rung — 'you just need more data' — was eliminated without ever varying the amount of data, and the repo's own later measurement contradicts the verdict
findings.evidence: RESULTS.md:16 `| **L1** | "you just need more data" | ✅ **eliminated** |`. The L1 audit (protocol lines 365-400) sweeps exactly three things: POD rank, bootstrap calibration, and choice of holdout split. `grep -n "frac|n_train|subsample|n_mat" run_l1.py` returns only `subsample=0.85` (an XGBoost column-sampling hyperparameter). No training-set-size axis exists anywhere in L1. learning_curve.py:1-6 states this in its own words: "L1 is recorded as eliminating that, and never measured it. ... The verdict therefore rests on a measurement that was not taken." learning_curve.log then measures it: field nRMSE 0.09292 (12 materials) -> 0.06931 (24) -> 0.05367 (36) -> 0.05094 (48), i.e. 1.82x and still falling at the last point.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the first rung of the ladder and the one whose elimination licenses every rung above it. A top-tier referee will read 'we eliminated more-data' and ask for the learning curve on the first pass; finding the project's own script saying the measurement was never taken, and a log showing the curve has not saturated, is a reject. It is also the exact defect class the RETRACTIONS ledger exists to catch (cf. A17: 'The n-width was measured but never tested as an explanation'), and it is currently unrecorded in either Part A or Part B.
findings.fix: (a) Open a Part-A retraction now: 'L1 verdict "eliminated" is withdrawn pending a learning curve.' (b) Finish learning_curve.py — the run is incomplete (see separate finding) — and run the same material-count axis in L1's OWN function class (POD+xgb at 64 modes) so the curve is comparable to L1's table, not only to the warp frame. (c) Restate the rung honestly whichever way it lands: the defensible claim may be 'more materials help sub-linearly and cannot close a 33x gap' (fit an exponent to the curve and extrapolate the material count needed to reach the POD floor — that number is itself a headline). (d) The 240-material scale-up dataset in data/parametric_scale is the right instrument; it is currently ~1457/4080 files with no manifest.

findings.title: RESULTS.md contains no L4/L4b section at all, and its L4 summary row states a verdict contradicted by the project's own strongest single result
findings.evidence: `grep -n "^## " RESULTS.md` lists L0, physics, n-width, L1, L2, L3, L5, co-moving, two-wave, L7, degeneracies, L6 — there is no L4 heading. The only L4 content is the table row at line 19: `| **L4** | "add the PDE residual" | ✅ **no difference** on the material axis |`. The protocol's L4b section (lines 1026-1101) reports the opposite emphasis and much more: `data-only TIME 0.1425 -> 0.0124  11.5x  CI [+0.1139, +0.1438]` for hard output bounds, and `bounded TIME 0.0124 -> 0.0194  1.6x WORSE  CI [-0.0112, -0.0020]` for the physics penalty. I confirmed the corrected values from results/l4b_time_corrected.json: unbounded/data_only 0.14248, unbounded/pi_gradnorm 0.06392, bounded/data_only 0.01236, bounded/pi_gradnorm 0.01936. CONTINUE_HERE.md:56 calls hard bounds 'the best single intervention'.
findings.why_it_matters: The running summary — the document a co-author or referee reads to learn what the study found — omits the intervention with the largest measured effect anywhere in the study (11.5x) and the only clean interaction result (structure helps, the same fact as a penalty hurts). Drafting an abstract from RESULTS.md today would omit the paper's best positive finding and would assert a null on L4 that the evidence refines rather than supports. It also makes the three governing documents mutually inconsistent on a headline verdict, which is the failure mode this project's process is designed to prevent.
findings.fix: Add a full `## L4/L4b` section to RESULTS.md carrying the 2x2 table, the three bound-vs-penalty CIs, and the interaction statement verbatim from protocol lines 1036-1090, and rewrite line 19 as `| **L4/L4b** | "add the PDE residual" | ✅ axis-specific — helps on time when structure is absent (2.2x), HURTS once hard bounds exist (1.6x); no effect on the material axis |`. Add a row for hard output bounds, which is currently not represented in the ladder table at all despite being the largest effect measured.
