2. `pdf.fonttype = 3` in all seven PDFs (confirmed by `/Type3` in the font objects). Two lines of rcParams.
3. Fig4: pixel census proves zero data-area pixels carry the `train` or `novel_condition` legend colours; the dominant dot colour rgb(190,132,79) is an alpha-composite matching no legend entry.

## Proposed main-text figure set for the new paper (8 figures)

The narrative is: *a verified reference -> a pre-registered ladder -> six hypotheses killed, one prediction refuted -> the obstruction located -> a coordinate change that removes it, with the remaining prize quantified.* Author every figure at exactly 3.46 in (single) or 7.09 in (double) column width, Okabe-Ito palette, one fixed colour per method across the whole paper, bold corner panel labels a/b/c, 7 pt text.

**F1 - The falsification ladder (schematic + verdict strip).** NEW. Single column. Left: eight rungs L0-L7 as a vertical stack, each row carrying the hypothesis in plain words, the pre-registered failure condition, and a coloured verdict chip (eliminated / refuted / not supported / verified). Right: a shared log axis showing every rung's best novel-material nRMSE as a dot, plus the POD floor as a black dashed rule, so the reader sees eight interventions all landing in the 0.048-0.073 band while the bound sits at 0.0015. Data: RESULTS.md ladder table + best arm per rung. **Takeaway: the ladder was pre-registered, it was executed, and nothing on it moved the number.** This is the figure that makes the paper a falsification study rather than a negative-results dump, and it does not exist.

**F2 - The system, and why it is hard.** Merges old Fig1 + Fig2. Double column, 2x3. (a) q*/q_max vs RH, Type V vs matched-q_max/matched-dH Langmuir, AWH operating window shaded. (b) dq*/dRH, log y, same two curves. (c) Exit curve c/c_in vs t/t_stoich for the Type V case, with t(0.1) and t(0.9) marked and the two waves annotated. (d) The c(z,t) field, q/q_max on a shared 0-1 scale, rasterized, with t_lo(z) and t_hi(z) overlaid in white. (e) The same field for a material at the other end of the wave-separation range. (f) Histogram of t(0.9)-t(0.1) across all 988 runs, spanning [0.025, 0.992] - the 40x range. **Takeaway: the isotherm form creates two waves whose separation varies 40x, which is the whole difficulty.** Panels (e) and (f) are what make the two-wave warp inevitable rather than arbitrary. Non-dimensionalise throughout, which also retires the MOF-303 placeholder exposure.

**F3 - Dataset design and coverage.** Rebuild of Fig4. Double column, 1x4. (a) 60 materials in (step_rh, n) with 48 train filled circles and 12 held-out open squares, alpha=1, marginal rugs. (b) The same 60 in (q_max, k_LDF). (c) The 17 operating conditions in (T_in, RH_in) with held-out conditions marked - the condition split belongs here, not on material axes. (d) Distribution of the derived Damkohler number with the sampled range 155-3885 (median 626) shown against the informative Da ~ 1-50 band. **Takeaway: the design is a genuine material-extrapolation test, and panel (d) discloses the k_LDF sampling limitation (open item 6) rather than waiting for a referee to find it.** Volunteering (d) converts a weakness into evidence of care.

**F4 - L1-L3: three eliminations.** Merges old Fig5A + Fig6. Double column, 1x3. (a) Four L1 arms as ratio-to-POD-floor on a linear axis (33.3, 33.5, 40.3, 46.4) with absolute nRMSE printed, floor at 1.0. (b) L2 capacity sweep, train and novel with seed bands, log y, floor as a black rule, annotated 'train falls 41x; novel flat to 15%'. (c) L3 families at matched parameters, three budgets, error bars, with the significance count (8/9) stated in-panel. **Takeaway: more data, more capacity and a better basis are all inert; the ordering MLP > RBF-KAN > Chebyshev-KAN is stable at every budget.**

**F5 - L4, L6, L7: physics, structure, and the classical control.** NEW. Double column, 1x3. (a) L4/L4b as a slope chart: nRMSE on the time axis 0.1425 -> 0.0639 with the residual loss, and 0.0124 -> 0.0194 once hard bounds exist, with the 11.5x hard-bounds intervention marked - the axis-specific result needs a picture and has none. (b) L6: joint vs separate vs separate_noeq as dot-and-CI on c, q and dt50, with the +0.0147 difference and its CI [-0.0155, +0.0450] straddling zero shown explicitly, plus an inset of the k_LDF identifiability scatter (R2 = -0.61). (c) L7: exit-curve nRMSE for rf vs Klinkenberg vs constant-pattern vs equilibrium-shock, with the POD floor, and dt50 error on a twin axis. **Takeaway: physics-as-a-loss is axis-specific and hard bounds dominate it; the primary pre-registered hypothesis H1 is not supported, with the cause measured; learning is nonetheless justified at 3.2x over the best closed form.** Panel (b) is the paper's primary hypothesis and currently has no figure at all.

**F6 - L5: the operator refutation and where the obstruction lives.** Rebuild of old Fig7, with the fill data merged. Double column, 2x2. (a) POD floor falling 28.7x against DeepONet flat, over the FULL lr grid including 3e-3, with the gap arrow (recomputed to 55x at the corrected 0.0275). (b) Basis error, DeepONet, and the k-mode-oracle sweep (true coefficients on the first k modes, predicted beyond) so the reader sees the curve cross DeepONet's level at k ~ 4-5 - this converts the current unbounded green line into an actual measurement. (c) Per-mode R2 of the params -> coefficient map, all 128 modes on log x, green/grey encoding retained. (d) An inset or margin panel: best-per-lr at p=128, showing the optimum is interior to the grid. **Takeaway: the pre-registered n-width prediction is refuted, the baseline was tuned to its optimum, and the binding constraint is the parameter -> coefficient map beyond ~5 modes.** Move DeepOKAN collapse to the SI.

**F7 - The two-wave warp.** NEW. This is the paper's punchline and has no figure. Double column, 2x3. (a) Schematic: one field in (z,t) and the same field in (z,sigma) with sigma = (t - t_lo)/(t_hi - t_lo), both fronts vertical after warping. (b) POD spectra in three frames - fixed, single warp L=0.5, two-wave 0.05-0.95 - with the 99.9% ranks 31 / 102 / 13 marked. (c) Oracle-warp nRMSE vs shape-basis size p for all three level pairs (0.10-0.90, 0.05-0.95, 0.20-0.80), showing flatness in p (0.02053 -> 0.02027) and showing the excluded 0.20-0.80 pair with its interpolation floor flagged - report the forking path, do not hide it. (d) Warp predictability: predicted vs true t_lo and t_hi on novel materials, R2 = +0.895 / +0.919, with the identity line. (e) The payoff curve from warp_predict.json: nRMSE vs alpha (warp-error interpolation), 0.0233 at alpha=0 rising to 0.0508 at alpha=1, with the fixed-frame 0.0510 as a rule - this single panel quantifies the entire remaining prize. (f) Oracle vs predicted vs fixed-frame vs DeepONet as four bars with the 2.17x headroom bracketed. **Takeaway: writing the field in two-wave coordinates collapses the n-width from 31 to 13 modes and gets POD-plus-GBM to 0.0203, beating every learned arm in the ladder; the entire gain is currently consumed by front-location error, and the remaining prize is 2.17x.**

**F8 - The obstruction has moved.** NEW, single column. A before/after diagram: through L1-L5 the obstruction is 'the parameter -> coefficient map is unlearnable beyond ~5 modes' (unaddressable by any architecture, six interventions tried and failed); after the coordinate change it is 'two smooth monotone 1-D curves are not located accurately enough' (a well-posed regression with a measured 2.17x prize and a stated target). Overlay the learning-curve result - error falling 1.82x, 0.0929 -> 0.0509, as training materials go 12 -> 48 and not saturating - because that is the concrete next lever and it partially qualifies the L1 verdict on the material axis. **Takeaway: the paper ends by handing the field a better-posed problem with a priced solution, not by reporting a null.**

**SI figures:** L0 verification as a horizontal dot plot (old Fig3, promoted only if space allows); the full n-width spectra with per-channel exponents and bootstrap CIs (old Fig5B); DeepOKAN collapse with the width/p confound stated (old Fig7D); the learning curves on both axes; the single-front co-moving refutation in full; the palette CVD check; grid-convergence and mass-balance.

## Proposed main-text table set (5 tables)

**T1 - Model and parameters.** Governing equations (mass, energy, LDF), Danckwerts BCs, the Do-Do dual-term Type V closure, and every parameter with its symbol, value or sampled range, units, and a provenance column with three levels: *derived*, *literature (cited)*, *literature-range placeholder (uncited)*. Every MOF-303 number goes in the third class, explicitly. This table is how retraction A4 stops being a liability - a referee who sees the provenance column volunteered will trust the rest of the paper more, not less.

**T2 - L0 verification.** Four closed-form checks, what each isolates, the measured error, the pre-registered gate threshold, pass/fail; plus mass-balance closure (0.050%) and grid convergence (0.055% / 0.323% at N_z = 2000). Add a row for the honest speed reference: 4.2 s/condition at N_z = 2000, own solver, same hardware (open item 5).

**T3 - The ladder ledger.** One row per rung: hypothesis in plain words; the pre-registered failure condition quoted verbatim from 03_LADDER_PROTOCOL.md with its line number; arms and seeds; the metric and split; the measured result with CI; verdict. This table IS the paper's methodological contribution and should be its most-cited object. Nothing like it appears in the current draft.

**T4 - L5 operator sweep.** Family x p x lr, mean +/- SD over 3 seeds on the novel-material split, with the POD floor and the ratio-to-floor per row, the full merged lr grid including 3e-3, and a collapse-count column. State explicitly that width is set by parameter matching and is collinear with p.

**T5 - Frames.** Fixed / single-warp (L = 0.1, 0.5, 0.9) / two-wave (0.10-0.90, 0.05-0.95, 0.20-0.80). Columns: modes for 90/99/99.9/99.99%, interpolation floor, oracle-warp nRMSE, predicted-warp nRMSE, warp R2 (lo/hi), and an inclusion flag with the exclusion reason for 0.20-0.80. This is the table a reader will actually use to reproduce the result.

**SI tables:** full hyperparameter grids per rung; seeds, CI method and calibrated alpha per rung; L7 classical baselines with cost per curve; the retraction ledger (17 Part-A + 23 Part-B) - print it, it is the paper's strongest credibility asset and it belongs in the SI where referees will find it.

## Production checklist that will otherwise bounce this at the journal

Type 3 fonts (all 7 PDFs); the 39 MB unrasterised mesh; text below 5 pt at column width (Fig6 at 4.4 pt, Fig7 at 4.8 pt); no figure authored to a column width; `bbox_inches='tight'` making the final size unpredictable; three incompatible panel-labelling conventions; three different palettes; a CVD collision at dE = 3.2 inside Fig7B; PNGs at 300 dpi where 600 is required for combination art; non-deterministic PDF CreationDate.
